```{r define-universe}
p_cutoff <- 0.05

# Extract significant genes from your exposure and time:exposure interaction contrasts
# in this case, we don't care about genes that are only significant wrt time
sig_exposure <- rownames(subset(res_exposure, padj < p_cutoff))
sig_interaction <- rownames(subset(res_interaction, padj < p_cutoff))

if (exists("res_time")) {
  sig_time <- rownames(subset(res_time, padj < p_cutoff))
  total_raw_sig <- length(unique(c(sig_time, sig_exposure, sig_interaction)))
  message("Total significant genes in global model: ", total_raw_sig)
}

# define background universe
# here it's genes that are significant with respect to exposure and/or time:exposure interaction
treatment_universe_full <- unique(c(sig_exposure, sig_interaction))

message("Treatment universe: ", length(treatment_universe_full), " genes.")

if (length(treatment_universe_full) == 0) {
  message("Warning: you don't have any genes")
}
```

```{r test-housekeeping-genes}

# 1. Define both term lists
terms_original <- c("ribosomal protein", "rRNA", "5S", "16S", "23S", "sigma factor", "RNA polymerase")
terms_modified <- c("ribosomal", "rRNA", "tRNA", "transfer RNA", "5S", "16S", "23S", "sigma factor", "RNA polymerase", "rpoA", "rpoB", "rpoC", "ribonuclease P", "tmRNA")

# 2. Count genes removed by the original method (using 'Product')
count_original <- anno_operon_clean %>%
  filter(str_detect(Product, paste(terms_original, collapse = "|"))) %>%
  nrow()

# 3. Count genes removed by the modified method (with case-insensitivity)
count_modified <- anno_operon_clean %>%
  filter(str_detect(Product, regex(paste(terms_modified, collapse = "|"), ignore_case = TRUE))) %>%
  nrow()

# 4. Get the total starting gene count
total_genes <- length(treatment_universe_full)

# 5. Create the comparison dataframe
comparison_table <- data.frame(
  Filter_Version = c("Original List", "Modified List (Expanded)"),
  Genes_Stripped = c(count_original, count_modified),
  Percent_Removed = c(
    paste0(round((count_original / total_genes) * 100, 2), "%"),
    paste0(round((count_modified / total_genes) * 100, 2), "%")
  ),
  Remaining_Universe = c(total_genes - count_original, total_genes - count_modified)
)

# 6. Output the table
print(comparison_table)
```

```{r test-housekeeping-gene-overview}
# 1. Define the terms
terms_original <- c("ribosomal protein", "rrna", "5s", "16s", "23s", "sigma factor", "rna polymerase")
terms_modified <- c("ribosomal", "rrna", "tRNA", "transfer RNA", "5s", "16s", "23s", "sigma factor", "rna polymerase", "rpoa", "rpob", "rpoc", "ribonuclease p", "tmrna")

# 2. Get unique genes caught by each method
genes_original <- anno_operon_clean %>%
  filter(str_detect(tolower(Product), paste(terms_original, collapse = "|"))) %>%
  pull(Gene) %>% 
  unique()

genes_modified <- anno_operon_clean %>%
  filter(str_detect(tolower(Product), paste(terms_modified, collapse = "|"))) %>%
  pull(Gene) %>% 
  unique()

# 3. Isolate the genes unique to the modified list
genes_only_in_modified <- setdiff(genes_modified, genes_original)

# 4. Pull the clean, distinct gene-to-product mapping
diff_table <- anno_operon_clean %>%
  filter(Gene %in% genes_only_in_modified) %>%
  select(Gene, Product) %>%
  distinct(Gene, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  arrange(Product)

# 5. Print directly to console
print(as.data.frame(diff_table))
```

I'm keeping tRNA and transfer RNAs because amino acid pathways are involved with our response
And this potentially gives us information about the tbox/riboswitch transcription control

"Ribosomal" is too broad - it's catching non-housekeeping genes. 30/50/70S are more involved with proteins as well


```{r clean-universe}
housekeeping_terms <- c(
  "\\b5s\\b", "\\b16s\\b", "\\b23s\\b",        # Structural RNAs (exact word match)
  "rrna",     # Pure structural/transport RNAs
  "ribosomal protein",                         # Catch the structural proteins only
  "^ribosomal large subunit$",                 # Strips if it's JUST the structural label
  "^ribosomal small subunit$",
  "sigma factor", "rna polymerase"             # Transcription core
)

# Filter out genes based on the 'Product' column (ignoring case for safety)
structural_noise_genes <- anno_operon_clean %>%
  filter(stringr::str_detect(
    Product, 
    stringr::regex(paste(housekeeping_terms, collapse = "|"), ignore_case = TRUE)
  )) %>%
  pull(Gene)

# Refine universe
treatment_universe <- setdiff(treatment_universe_full, structural_noise_genes)

# Print summary messages
message("Structural genes removed: ", length(structural_noise_genes))
message("Refined treatment universe: ", length(treatment_universe))
```

```{r}
# 1. Pull the data from your VSD object using your clean treatment universe
mat_filtered <- assay(vsd_06_24)[rownames(vsd_06_24) %in% treatment_universe, ]

# 2. Scale row-wise (by gene) so c-means tracks trajectories, not absolute counts
mat_scaled <- t(scale(t(mat_filtered)))

# 3. Quick loop-safety check (drops genes with 0 variance across your samples)
nan_rows <- which(rowSums(is.na(mat_scaled)) > 0)
if(length(nan_rows) > 0) {
  message("Dropped ", length(nan_rows), " genes from mat_scaled due to zero variance.")
  mat_scaled <- mat_scaled[-nan_rows, ]
}
```




```{r find-optimal-clusters}
# define your parameters
k_range <- 2:10
m_parameter <- 2.0
n_obs <- nrow(mat_scaled)

# Initialize storage
results_list <- list()

# generate silhouette, fpc, and xie-beni indexes for the range of cluster numbers
for (i in seq_along(k_range)) {
  k_test <- k_range[i]

  set.seed(42)
  fcm_res <- e1071::cmeans(mat_scaled, centers = k_test, m = m_parameter, method = "cmeans")

  # --- Metric A: Silhouette Width ---
  # Based on hard assignments from the highest membership
  hard_clusters <- apply(fcm_res$membership, 1, which.max)
  sil_res <- cluster::silhouette(hard_clusters, dist(mat_scaled))
  avg_sil <- mean(sil_res[, "sil_width"])

  # --- Metric B: Fuzzy Partition Coefficient (FPC) ---
  # Measures "fuzziness" overlap; closer to 1.0 means cleaner separation
  fpc_val <- sum(fcm_res$membership^2) / n_obs

  # --- Metric C: Xie-Beni Index ---
  # Ratio of compactness to separation; lower values are better
  u <- fcm_res$membership
  v <- fcm_res$centers

  numerator <- 0
  for (j in 1:k_test) {
    diffs <- sweep(mat_scaled, 2, v[j, ], "-")
    sq_dists <- rowSums(diffs^2)
    numerator <- numerator + sum((u[, j]^m_parameter) * sq_dists)
  }
  min_center_dist_sq <- min(dist(v)^2)
  xb_index <- numerator / (n_obs * min_center_dist_sq)

  # Store all in list
  results_list[[i]] <- data.frame(
    K                = k_test,
    Silhouette_Width = avg_sil,
    FPC              = fpc_val,
    Xie_Beni_Index   = xb_index
  )
}

validation_ledger <- bind_rows(results_list)

# plot the metrics so you can chose the number of clusters
# for fpc and silhouette, we want to maximize the number - look for plateaus followed by dropoffs
# xb can be eaiser to find inflection points - look for the last number before a sharp spike
plot_df <- validation_ledger %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -K, names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Value") %>%
  # Reorder factors for consistent stacking
  mutate(Metric = factor(Metric, levels = c("FPC", "Silhouette_Width", "Xie_Beni_Index")))

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = K, y = Value)) +
  geom_line(aes(color = Metric), size = 1, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Metric), size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~Metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = k_range) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FPC" = "#2C3E50", "Silhouette_Width" = "#2980B9", "Xie_Beni_Index" = "#C0392B")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Cluster Validity Triangulation",
    subtitle = "Goal: Maximize FPC & Silhouette | Minimize Xie-Beni Index",
    x = "Number of Clusters (K)",
    y = "Score"
  )
```
Sometimes the output from the indexes is inconsistent or unclear
Here we're running potential Ks to see what the output looks like

```{r test-cluster-numbers}
# list of potential cluster numbers
target_ks <- c(4,7, 8, 9,10)
# minimum score threshold for keeping genes as part of the cluster
score_thresh <- 0.25
# genes with high log2fcs tend to have poor cluster scores
# this sets the log2fc recovery threshold
r_thresh <- 1


# define function

run_fuzzy_pipeline <- function(k_val, input_matrix, base_df, rescue_thresh = r_thresh) {
  set.seed(42)
  fcm_out <- e1071::cmeans(input_matrix, centers = k_val, m = 2.0, method = "cmeans")

  df_res <- base_df %>%
    rownames_to_column("Gene") %>%
    mutate(
      cluster = as.factor(fcm_out$cluster),
      membership_score = apply(fcm_out$membership, 1, max),
      is_driver = if_else(
        membership_score > score_thresh | abs(model_LFC_06h) >= rescue_thresh | abs(model_LFC_24h) >= rescue_thresh,
        "High-Confidence",
        "Background"
      )
    )
  return(df_res)
}

# prepare matrix
df_2d_base <- data.frame(
  model_LFC_06h = res_06h_exposure[treatment_universe, "log2FoldChange"],
  model_LFC_24h = res_24h_exposure[treatment_universe, "log2FoldChange"],
  row.names     = treatment_universe
)
mat_scaled <- scale(as.matrix(df_2d_base))
```

```{r run-models}
# Store results in a list for easy access
model_results <- list()

for (k in target_ks) {
  message(sprintf("\n--- Cluster profiles  K = %d ---", k))

  # Run Pipeline
  df_final <- run_fuzzy_pipeline(k, mat_scaled, df_2d_base)
  model_results[[paste0("K", k)]] <- df_final

  # 1. Print Driver Confidence Table
  print(table(df_final$cluster, df_final$is_driver))

  # 2. Calculate and Print Cluster Profiles (Averages)
  profiles <- df_final %>%
    group_by(cluster) %>%
    summarize(
      count    = n(),
      mean_06h = mean(model_LFC_06h),
      mean_24h = mean(model_LFC_24h),
      avg_mem  = mean(membership_score)
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(abs(mean_06h)))

  print(profiles)
}
```

# Alt: extract outliers from around the oval 

let's use mahalanobis distance because it is an oval (euclidean assumes circle)

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(plotly)

q_cut <- 0.95

# ==============================================================================
# 1. OUTLIER CALCULATION & INTEGRATED LAYERING
# ==============================================================================
fc_matrix <- df_final_clusters %>%
  select(model_LFC_06h, model_LFC_24h) %>%
  as.matrix()

oval_center <- colMeans(fc_matrix)
oval_covariance <- cov(fc_matrix)

df_final_clusters$mahalanobis_dist <- mahalanobis(
  fc_matrix,
  center = oval_center,
  cov = oval_covariance
)

outlier_cutoff <- qchisq(p = q_cut, df = 2)

df_plot_data <- df_final_clusters %>%
  inner_join(color_map, by = "cluster") %>%
  mutate(
    is_outlier = if_else(mahalanobis_dist > outlier_cutoff, "Toxicant Outlier", "Normal Oval"),
    cluster_factor = factor(cluster)
  )

# PLOTLY-SAFE: Create a map using ONLY the vibrant base_colors for the manual scale
vibrant_dictionary <- df_plot_data %>%
  distinct(cluster_factor, base_color) %>%
  {
    setNames(as.character(.$base_color), as.character(.$cluster_factor))
  }

# ==============================================================================
# 2. PLOTLY-PROOF VISUALIZATION ENGINE
# ==============================================================================
p_static <- ggplot(df_plot_data, aes(
  x = model_LFC_06h,
  y = model_LFC_24h,
  color = cluster_factor, # Maps cleanly to the vibrant colors
  shape = is_outlier,
  text = paste0(
    "<b>Gene:</b> ", Gene, "<br>",
    "<b>Fuzzy Cluster:</b> ", cluster, "<br>",
    "<b>Membership Score:</b> ", round(membership_score, 3), "<br>",
    "<b>LFC 06h:</b> ", round(model_LFC_06h, 2), "<br>",
    "<b>LFC 24h:</b> ", round(model_LFC_24h, 2), "<br>",
    "<b>Oval Deviation (M-Dist):</b> ", round(mahalanobis_dist, 2), "<br>",
    "<b>Visual Layer:</b> ", is_outlier
  )
)) +

  # By using scale_alpha_manual, ggplot handles the transparency on the canvas
  # independently without letting plotly corrupt the legend colors
  geom_point(aes(size = is_outlier, alpha = is_outlier)) +
  xlim(-3, 3) +
  ylim(-3, 5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray60", size = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray60", size = 0.4) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dotted", color = "gray50", size = 0.4) +

  # Legend keys inherit these exact vibrant hex codes explicitly
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Cluster",
    values = vibrant_dictionary
  ) +

  # Define shapes and sizes
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Toxicant Outlier" = 19, "Normal Oval" = 19)) + # Use solid dots for both to protect legend display
  scale_size_manual(values = c("Toxicant Outlier" = 2.0, "Normal Oval" = 1.0)) +

  # ENFORCED TRANSPARENCY: Outliers are 100% solid, normal oval points drop to 15% ghost opacity
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("Toxicant Outlier" = 1.0, "Normal Oval" = 0.15)) +
  guides(
    shape = "none",
    size = "none",
    alpha = "none"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Globally Scaled Fuzzy Cohorts (K = ", k_used, ")"),
    subtitle = "Mathematical Outliers: Solid 100% opacity",
    x = "Log2 Fold Change at 06h (Initial Shock)",
    y = "Log2 Fold Change at 24h (Metabolic Shift)"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

# Convert to interactive plotly canvas wrapper
p_interactive <- ggplotly(p_static, tooltip = "text") %>%
  layout(yaxis = list(scaleanchor = "x", scaleratio = 1))

p_static
figname <- sprintf("mahalanobis_%.2f.png",q_cut)

ggsave(file.path(results_dir, figname))

p_interactive
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# 3. SELF-CONTAINED EXTRACTION & CSV EXPORT OF TOXICANT OUTLIERS
# ==============================================================================

# Recalculate the cutoff using your already defined q_cut
outlier_cutoff <- qchisq(p = q_cut, df = 2)

# Extract directly from the source data frame to avoid environment drops
df_outliers_extracted <- df_final_clusters %>%
  # Filter directly using the Mahalanobis distance metric
  filter(mahalanobis_dist > outlier_cutoff) %>%
  # Select and clean up the spreadsheet columns
  select(
    Gene, 
    cluster, 
    membership_score, 
    model_LFC_06h, 
    model_LFC_24h, 
    mahalanobis_dist
  ) %>%
  # Sort with the most extreme biological responses at the top
  arrange(desc(mahalanobis_dist))

# Construct filename and save
csv_name <- sprintf("toxicant_outliers_q%.2f_%.0fclust.csv", q_cut, k_final)
csv_path <- file.path(results_dir, csv_name)

write.csv(df_outliers_extracted, file = csv_path, row.names = FALSE)

# Print tracking message
message("Successfully exported ", nrow(df_outliers_extracted), " toxicant outliers to: ", csv_path)
```

# --- cut this here ---






```{r}
# 1. Extract the matrix of fold changes for the two axes
fc_matrix <- as.matrix(scatterplot_data[, c("log2FC_06h", "log2FC_24h")])

# 2. Compute the center and covariance matrix of your data
data_center <- colMeans(fc_matrix)
data_covariance <- cov(fc_matrix)

# 3. Calculate Mahalanobis distance for every gene
scatterplot_data$mahalanobis_dist <- mahalanobis(fc_matrix, center = data_center, cov = data_covariance)

# 4. Use a Chi-Square cutoff to define strict outliers (df = 2 for 2D space)
# p < 0.01 forces a high threshold, isolating true extreme outliers
cutoff_value <- qchisq(p = 0.99, df = 2)

toxicant_outliers <- scatterplot_data %>%
  filter(mahalanobis_dist > cutoff_value)
```

# Enrichment

This is modular, so select your annotation and lookup of interest
My annotations include KO, GO, COG, COG categories, as well as KEGG modules/pathways/reactions
For KEGG and COG I made lookup tsv files of the categories and their definitions
GO is a separate block of code because I had to query the API for the category definitions


Define databases based on the information in your annotations and structure of your lookup tables
```{r define-databases}
db_configs <- list(
  KO = list(
    db_label = "KO",
    database_tsv_path = "/mnt/work-drive/databases/COG-KEGG-data/KO-definitions.tsv",
    db_term_col = "KO",
    db_definition_col = "kDefinition"
  ),
  kPathway = list(
    db_label = "KEGG_Pathway",
    database_tsv_path = "/mnt/work-drive/databases/COG-KEGG-data/kegg-pathwaymaps.tsv",
    db_term_col = "pathway",
    db_definition_col = "kPathDef"
  ),
  kModule = list(
    db_label = "KEGG_Module",
    database_tsv_path = "/mnt/work-drive/databases/COG-KEGG-data/kegg-modules.tsv",
    db_term_col = "module",
    db_definition_col = "kModDef"
  ),
  kRxn = list(
    db_label = "KEGG_Reaction",
    database_tsv_path = "/mnt/work-drive/databases/COG-KEGG-data/kegg-reactions.tsv",
    db_term_col = "reaction",
    db_definition_col = "kReactionDef"
  ),
  COG = list(
    db_label = "COG",
    database_tsv_path = "/mnt/work-drive/databases/COG-KEGG-data/cog-def.tsv",
    db_term_col = "COG",
    db_definition_col = "cDef"
  ),
  COGcat = list(
    db_label = "COG_cat",
    database_tsv_path = "/mnt/work-drive/databases/COG-KEGG-data/cog_codes.tsv",
    db_term_col = "COG_code",
    db_definition_col = "cCodeDef"
  )
)
```


Here is where the enrichment analysis happens.
Select an annotation/database defined above, and your output thresholds.
This saves the data in three ways: by enrichment term, by gene, and as a +/- matrix.

```{r cluster-enrichment}
# ----- Definitions -----
target_db <- "COGcat" # Options: "KO", "kPathway", "kModule", "kRxn", "COG", "COGcat"

# Threshold variables for output table
qtable <- 0.3 # q threshold for out table
ptable <- 0.1 # p threshold for out table
clust_thresh <- 0.25 # cluster membership threshold

# subfolder for reshaped outputs
subfolder_dir <- file.path(results_dir, "reshaped_outputs")
if (!dir.exists(subfolder_dir)) dir.create(subfolder_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# keywords to filter out
housekeeping_terms <- c("ribosomal protein", "rRNA", "5S", "16S", "23S", "sigma factor", "RNA polymerase")
# -----


# Dynamically assign the four variables based on your target selection
db_label <- db_configs[[target_db]]$db_label
database_tsv_path <- db_configs[[target_db]]$database_tsv_path
db_term_col <- db_configs[[target_db]]$db_term_col
db_definition_col <- db_configs[[target_db]]$db_definition_col

# Load term definitions
clean_defs <- read.delim(database_tsv_path, sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  select(ID = !!sym(db_term_col), Description = !!sym(db_definition_col)) %>%
  distinct()

# Universe definition
# Get detectable background from DESeq2
raw_universe_genes <- rownames(dds)

# Split multi-term genes to one per row
t2g_base <- anno_operon_clean %>%
  filter(Gene %in% raw_universe_genes) %>%
  select(!!sym(db_label), Gene) %>%
  drop_na(!!sym(db_label))

if (db_label == "COG_cat") {
  t2g_split <- t2g_base %>%
    mutate(!!sym(db_label) := gsub("[ ,]", "", !!sym(db_label))) %>%
    separate_rows(!!sym(db_label), sep = "")
} else {
  # Fix: Use a regex pattern to catch commas even if they don't have spaces
  t2g_split <- t2g_base %>%
    separate_rows(!!sym(db_label), sep = ",\\s*")

  # For pathways, keep ONLY rows starting exactly with 'map' followed by digits
  if (target_db == "kPathway") {
    t2g_split <- t2g_split %>%
      filter(grepl("^map\\d+", !!sym(db_label)))
  }
}


# Filter out split gene-term pairs that match our housekeeping terms
t2g <- t2g_split %>%
  rename(ID = !!sym(db_label)) %>%
  left_join(clean_defs, by = "ID") %>%
  # Remove only the specific rows that match housekeeping terms
  filter(!grepl(paste(housekeeping_terms, collapse = "|"),
    Description,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )) %>%
  select(term_id = ID, gene_id = Gene) %>%
  filter(term_id != "" & term_id != "NA") %>%
  distinct()

# Our cosmos
universe_vector <- unique(t2g$gene_id)

# Import clusters
cluster_input <- df_final_clusters %>%
  filter(is_driver == "High-Confidence") %>% # Dynamically honors score + LFC rescues
  filter(Gene %in% universe_vector) %>%
  select(Gene, cluster)

n_clusters <- length(unique(cluster_input$cluster))

# Run cluster enrichment analysis
all_clusters <- sort(unique(cluster_input$cluster))
enrichment_results_list <- list()

for (clust_id in all_clusters) {
  current_cluster_genes <- cluster_input %>%
    filter(cluster == clust_id) %>%
    pull(Gene)

  if (length(intersect(current_cluster_genes, universe_vector)) > 0) {
    ego <- enricher(
      gene         = current_cluster_genes,
      universe     = universe_vector,
      TERM2GENE    = t2g,
      pvalueCutoff = ptable,
      qvalueCutoff = qtable,
      minGSSize    = 2,
      maxGSSize    = 500
    )

    if (!is.null(ego) && nrow(ego@result) > 0) {
      res_df <- as.data.frame(ego) %>%
        mutate(Analysis_Group = paste0("Cluster_", clust_id))
      enrichment_results_list[[as.character(clust_id)]] <- res_df
    }
  }
}

# Clean and save data
if (length(enrichment_results_list) > 0) {
  # generate the master base table with correct column order
  final_enrichment_df <- bind_rows(enrichment_results_list) %>%
    select(-any_of("Description")) %>%
    left_join(clean_defs, by = "ID") %>%
    select(Analysis_Group, ID, Description, Count, everything())


  # file naming pattern
  base_name <- sprintf("enrichment_%s_m%.2f-resc_c%d", db_label, clust_thresh, n_clusters)

  # Organized by enrichment term
  # =========================================================================
  original_out_path <- file.path(results_dir, paste0(base_name, ".tsv"))
  write.table(final_enrichment_df, original_out_path, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)

  # Organized by cluster, then gene
  tidy_long_df <- final_enrichment_df %>%
    # Split slash-separated genes into individual clean rows
    separate_rows(geneID, sep = "/") %>%
    rename(Gene_ID = geneID) %>%
    # Put Gene_ID right up front next to Analysis Group
    select(Analysis_Group, Gene_ID, ID, Description, everything()) %>%
    # Strict alphabetical/numerical sort by cluster, then by gene, then by significance
    arrange(Analysis_Group, Gene_ID, p.adjust)

  long_out_path <- file.path(subfolder_dir, paste0(base_name, "_long_by_gene.tsv"))
  write.table(tidy_long_df, long_out_path, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)

  # binary presence/absence matrix
  matrix_wide_df <- final_enrichment_df %>%
    # 1. Create a simple indicator flag for enrichment presence
    mutate(Enriched = 1) %>%
    # 2. Select only the core identifier metadata and our new columns
    select(ID, Description, Analysis_Group, Enriched) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    # 3. Pivot clusters into columns. Rows collapse down to unique IDs!
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = Analysis_Group,
      values_from = Enriched,
      values_fill = 0
    ) %>%
    # 4. Optional: sort by ID to make it easy to read alphabetically
    arrange(ID)

  wide_out_path <- file.path(subfolder_dir, paste0(base_name, "_cluster_profile_matrix.tsv"))
  write.table(matrix_wide_df, wide_out_path, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)

  # Console feedback
  message("Success! Exported three file variations:")
  message(sprintf("  -> Original Table: %s", basename(original_out_path)))
  message(sprintf("  -> Long Tidy (By Gene): %s", file.path("reshaped_outputs", basename(long_out_path))))
  message(sprintf("  -> Wide Profile Matrix: %s", file.path("reshaped_outputs", basename(wide_out_path))))
} else {
  message(sprintf("No enrichment found for %s, %d clusters with current parameters.", db_label, n_clusters))
}
```

```{r basic-dotplot, fig.width=8, fig.height=10}
# =========================================================================
# OPTIONAL VISUALIZATION: CLUSTER PROFILE HEATMAP / DOTPLOT
# =========================================================================

if (exists("final_enrichment_df") && nrow(final_enrichment_df) > 0) {
  # 1. Prepare data for plotting
  # We use the top 50 most significant terms if the table is massive,
  # ensuring the plot remains readable. Adjust 'max_terms' as needed.
  max_terms <- 50

  plot_data <- final_enrichment_df %>%
    group_by(Analysis_Group) %>%
    slice_min(order_by = p.adjust, n = 15, with_ties = FALSE) %>% # Top 15 per cluster
    ungroup() %>%
    distinct(ID, Description, Analysis_Group, p.adjust, Count) %>%
    # Create a clean label combining ID and Description
    mutate(Term_Label = sprintf("%s: %s", ID, substr(Description, 1, 50))) %>%
    # Order terms by their significance so the plot looks structured
    mutate(Term_Label = fct_reorder(Term_Label, p.adjust, .desc = TRUE))

  if (nrow(plot_data) > max_terms) {
    # If still too many terms globally, truncate to the top overall
    top_terms <- plot_data %>%
      group_by(Term_Label) %>%
      summarise(min_p = min(p.adjust)) %>%
      slice_min(order_by = min_p, n = max_terms, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
      pull(Term_Label)

    plot_data <- plot_data %>% filter(Term_Label %in% top_terms)
  }

  # 2. Build the Dotplot Matrix
  # This shows which clusters share pathways, scaled by gene count and colored by p-value
  enrich_plot <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = Term_Label)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = Count, color = -log10(p.adjust))) +
    scale_color_viridis_c(name = "-log10(p.adjust)", option = "magma", direction = 1) +
    scale_size_continuous(name = "Gene Count", range = c(3, 8)) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    labs(
      title = sprintf("Functional Enrichment Profile (%s)", target_db),
      subtitle = "Top enriched terms mapped across analysis groups",
      x = "Analysis Cluster",
      y = "Enriched Functional Term"
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray95"),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
      legend.position = "right"
    )

  # 3. Save the Plot Dynamically
  plot_out_name <- sprintf("enrichment_profile_%s_m%.2f.png", db_label, clust_thresh)
  plot_out_path <- file.path(results_dir, "reshaped_outputs", plot_out_name)

  # Adjust dynamic height based on the number of unique terms to prevent crowding
  dynamic_height <- max(5, length(unique(plot_data$Term_Label)) * 0.25)

  ggsave(
    filename = plot_out_path,
    plot = enrich_plot,
    width = 9,
    height = dynamic_height,
    dpi = 300,
    bg = "white"
  )

  message(sprintf("Visualization Success! Plot saved to: %s", file.path("reshaped_outputs", plot_out_name)))

  # Render the plot in RStudio console/notebook
  print(enrich_plot)
} else {
  message("Skipping visualization: No enrichment data available to plot.")
}
```

```{r hierarchical-dotplot, fig.width=9, fig.height=11}
# =========================================================================
# OPTIONAL VISUALIZATION: HIERARCHICALLY CLUSTERED DOT PLOT
# =========================================================================

if (exists("final_enrichment_df") && nrow(final_enrichment_df) > 0) {
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 1: Prep Continuous Matrix & Run Clustering to Get Axis Orders
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  matrix_prep <- final_enrichment_df %>%
    mutate(Signal = -log10(p.adjust)) %>%
    mutate(Row_Label = sprintf("%s: %s", ID, substr(Description, 1, 40))) %>%
    select(Row_Label, Analysis_Group, Signal) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Analysis_Group, values_from = Signal, values_fill = 0)

  # Filter down to top 50 rows based on variance to keep the dot plot clean
  if (nrow(matrix_prep) > 50) {
    row_vars <- apply(as.matrix(matrix_prep[, -1]), 1, var)
    matrix_prep <- matrix_prep[order(-row_vars)[1:50], ]
  }

  # Convert to pure matrix format for clustering calculations
  clust_matrix <- as.matrix(matrix_prep[, -1])
  rownames(clust_matrix) <- matrix_prep$Row_Label

  # Extract hierarchical order for Rows (Pathways)
  row_hc <- hclust(dist(clust_matrix, method = "euclidean"), method = "complete")
  ordered_pathways <- rownames(clust_matrix)[row_hc$order]

  # Extract hierarchical order for Columns (Analysis Groups/Clusters)
  col_hc <- hclust(dist(t(clust_matrix), method = "euclidean"), method = "complete")
  ordered_clusters <- colnames(clust_matrix)[col_hc$order]

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 2: Filter and Reorder Plotting Data Based on the Clustering Trees
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  plot_data_clustered <- final_enrichment_df %>%
    mutate(Row_Label = sprintf("%s: %s", ID, substr(Description, 1, 40))) %>%
    filter(Row_Label %in% ordered_pathways) %>%
    # Convert axes to factors and explicitly dictate the hierarchical levels
    mutate(
      Analysis_Group = factor(Analysis_Group, levels = ordered_clusters),
      Row_Label      = factor(Row_Label, levels = ordered_pathways)
    )

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 3: Draw the Hierarchical Dot Plot
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  hier_dotplot <- ggplot(plot_data_clustered, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = Row_Label)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = Count, color = -log10(p.adjust))) +
    scale_color_viridis_c(name = "-log10(p.adjust)", option = "magma", direction = 1) +
    scale_size_continuous(name = "Gene Count", range = c(3, 8)) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    labs(
      title = sprintf("Hierarchical Dot Plot Profile (%s)", target_db),
      subtitle = "Axes arranged dynamically by profile pattern similarity",
      x = "Analysis Clusters (Clustered)",
      y = "Enriched Functional Terms (Clustered)"
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray95"),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)
    )

  # Save to PNG via ggsave
  dot_out_name <- sprintf("enrichment_hierarchical_dotplot_%s_m%.2f.png", db_label, clust_thresh)
  dot_out_path <- file.path(results_dir, "reshaped_outputs", dot_out_name)

  dynamic_height <- max(5, length(ordered_pathways) * 0.22)

  ggsave(
    filename = dot_out_path,
    plot = hier_dotplot,
    width = 9,
    height = dynamic_height,
    dpi = 300,
    bg = "white"
  )

  message(sprintf("Hierarchical Dot Plot Success! Saved to: %s", file.path("reshaped_outputs", dot_out_name)))
  print(hier_dotplot)
} else {
  message("Skipping Visualization: No matching enrichment data available.")
}
```

```{r hierarchical-heatmap-presence-absense, fig.width=7, fig.height=9}
# =========================================================================
# OPTIONAL VISUALIZATION: HIERARCHICAL CLUSTERING HEATMAP
# =========================================================================

if (exists("matrix_wide_df") && nrow(matrix_wide_df) > 0) {
  # We use pheatmap because it handles dataframes elegantly and builds clean dendrograms
  if (!requireNamespace("pheatmap", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pheatmap")
  library(pheatmap)
  library(dplyr)

  # 1. Prepare a clean numeric matrix for clustering
  # We use the wide matrix generated in FORMAT B
  heatmap_matrix <- matrix_wide_df %>%
    # Use the pathway Description as the row name so it shows up on the plot
    mutate(Row_Label = sprintf("%s: %s", ID, substr(Description, 1, 40))) %>%
    select(-ID, -Description) %>%
    # Ensure there are no duplicate row names
    distinct(Row_Label, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    tibble::column_to_rownames("Row_Label") %>%
    as.matrix()

  # 2. Filter down if the matrix is completely unreadable (Optional)
  # Only plot terms that are active in at least one cluster
  heatmap_matrix <- heatmap_matrix[rowSums(heatmap_matrix) > 0, , drop = FALSE]

  # Safety check: Cap the number of rows if it's too massive for a single PDF page
  if (nrow(heatmap_matrix) > 60) {
    message("Notice: Truncating heatmap to the top 60 terms with the most cluster overlaps for readability.")
    term_variance <- rowSums(heatmap_matrix)
    heatmap_matrix <- heatmap_matrix[order(-term_variance)[1:60], , drop = FALSE]
  }

  # 3. Define the Graphic Output Path
  heatmap_out_name <- sprintf("enrichment_heatmap_%s_m%.2f.pdf", db_label, clust_thresh)
  heatmap_out_path <- file.path(results_dir, "reshaped_outputs", heatmap_out_name)

  # 4. Draw and Save the Clustered Heatmap
  # We use a PDF output here because text labels scale perfectly without pixelating
  pdf(file = heatmap_out_path, width = 8, height = max(6, nrow(heatmap_matrix) * 0.22))

  pheatmap(
    mat = heatmap_matrix,
    color = c("#f0f0f0", "#2b8cbe"), # Light gray for 0 (Absence), Deep blue for 1 (Enriched)
    legend_breaks = c(0, 1),
    legend_labels = c("Not Enriched", "Enriched"),
    cluster_rows = TRUE, # Dynamically cluster pathways by profile similarity
    cluster_cols = TRUE, # Dynamically cluster analysis groups by pathway profile
    clustering_distance_rows = "binary", # 'binary' distance is mathematically best for 1/0 matrices
    clustering_distance_cols = "binary",
    clustering_method = "complete",
    border_color = "white",
    fontsize_row = 8,
    fontsize_col = 10,
    main = sprintf("Hierarchical Profiles: %s Enrichment", target_db)
  )

  dev.off() # Close the file stream

  message(sprintf("Heatmap Success! Clustered architecture saved to: %s", file.path("reshaped_outputs", heatmap_out_name)))
} else {
  message("Skipping Heatmap: Wide profile matrix data is missing or empty.")
}
```

```{r clustered-heatmap-continuous, fig.width=8, fig.height=10}
# =========================================================================
# OPTIONAL VISUALIZATION: DYNAMIC CONTINUOUS CLUSTERING HEATMAP

if (exists("final_enrichment_df") && nrow(final_enrichment_df) > 0) {
  library(pheatmap)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)

  # 1. Transform the dynamic bubble-plot data into a continuous numeric matrix
  continuous_matrix <- final_enrichment_df %>%
    # Calculate the strength of enrichment (-log10 of adjusted p-value)
    mutate(Signal_Strength = -log10(p.adjust)) %>%
    # Truncate long descriptions so the plot labels look clean
    mutate(Row_Label = sprintf("%s: %s", ID, substr(Description, 1, 40))) %>%
    select(Row_Label, Analysis_Group, Signal_Strength) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    # Pivot out clusters into columns, filling missing combinations with 0 (no signal)
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = Analysis_Group,
      values_from = Signal_Strength,
      values_fill = 0
    ) %>%
    tibble::column_to_rownames("Row_Label") %>%
    as.matrix()

  # 2. Filter down to the most informative terms to avoid visual crowding
  # We select the top 50 terms that show the highest variance across your clusters
  if (nrow(continuous_matrix) > 50) {
    message("Notice: Subsetting heatmap to the top 50 terms with the highest profile variance.")
    row_variances <- apply(continuous_matrix, 1, var)
    continuous_matrix <- continuous_matrix[order(-row_variances)[1:50], , drop = FALSE]
  }

  # 3. Define output path
  heatmap_continuous_name <- sprintf("enrichment_continuous_heatmap_%s_m%.2f.pdf", db_label, clust_thresh)
  heatmap_continuous_path <- file.path(results_dir, "reshaped_outputs", heatmap_continuous_name)

  # 4. Generate the plot
  pdf(file = heatmap_continuous_path, width = 8, height = max(6, nrow(continuous_matrix) * 0.22))

  pheatmap(
    mat = continuous_matrix,
    # Using a continuous color gradient (Light gray -> Orange -> Deep Purple)
    color = colorRampPalette(c("#f0f0f0", "#fe9929", "#800026"))(50),
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    cluster_cols = TRUE,
    clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean", # Euclidean is ideal for continuous gradients!
    clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
    clustering_method = "complete",
    border_color = "white",
    fontsize_row = 8,
    fontsize_col = 10,
    main = sprintf("Clustered Enrichment Intensity [-log10(p.adj)]: %s", target_db)
  )

  dev.off()

  message(sprintf("Continuous Heatmap Success! Saved to: %s", file.path("reshaped_outputs", heatmap_continuous_name)))
} else {
  message("Skipping Continuous Heatmap: No data available.")
}
```

```{r !!!go-enrichment}
# ----- Define Variables -----
qtable <- 0.6 # q threshold for out table
ptable <- 0.2 # p threshold for out table
clust_thresh <- 0.25 # cluster membership threshold

target_db <- "GO_bak"

# -----

# Define background from detectable genes
raw_universe_genes <- rownames(dds)

# Map genes to GO terms
t2g <- anno_operon_clean %>%
  filter(Gene %in% raw_universe_genes) %>%
  # Use dplyr:: explicitly here
  dplyr::select(!!sym(target_db), Gene) %>%
  drop_na(!!sym(target_db)) %>%
  separate_rows(!!sym(target_db), sep = ", ") %>%
  filter(!!sym(target_db) != "" & !!sym(target_db) != "NA") %>%
  rename(term_id = !!sym(target_db), gene_id = Gene) %>%
  distinct()
universe_vector <- unique(t2g$gene_id)

# Run enrichment
cluster_input <- df_final_clusters %>%
  filter(is_driver == "High-Confidence" & Gene %in% universe_vector)
# filter(membership_score >= clust_thresh & Gene %in% universe_vector)

all_clusters <- sort(unique(cluster_input$cluster))
enrich_list <- list()

message("Starting GO Enrichment for ", length(all_clusters), " clusters...")

for (clust_id in all_clusters) {
  current_genes <- cluster_input %>%
    filter(cluster == clust_id) %>%
    pull(Gene)

  ego <- enricher(
    gene         = current_genes,
    universe     = universe_vector,
    TERM2GENE    = t2g,
    pvalueCutoff = ptable,
    qvalueCutoff = qtable,
    minGSSize    = 2
  )

  if (!is.null(ego) && nrow(ego@result) > 0) {
    enrich_list[[as.character(clust_id)]] <- as.data.frame(ego) %>%
      mutate(Analysis_Group = paste0("Cluster_", clust_id))
  }
}

# lookup term definitions
library(GO.db)

if (length(enrich_list) > 0) {
  all_go_res <- bind_rows(enrich_list)
  unique_go_ids <- unique(all_go_res$ID)

  message("Mapping metadata for ", length(unique_go_ids), " unique GO terms...")

  # Explicitly use AnnotationDbi for the database query
  go_metadata_df <- AnnotationDbi::select(
    x       = GO.db,
    keys    = unique_go_ids,
    columns = c("GOID", "TERM", "DEFINITION"),
    keytype = "GOID"
  ) %>%
    dplyr::rename(ID = GOID, GO_Name = TERM, GO_Definition = DEFINITION)

  # merge and save
  final_go_df <- all_go_res %>%
    dplyr::left_join(go_metadata_df, by = "ID")

  # Force-verify that geneID exists before dropping columns,
  # or find its exact spelling if clusterProfiler output changed.
  if (!"geneID" %in% colnames(final_go_df) & "gene_id" %in% colnames(final_go_df)) {
    final_go_df <- final_go_df %>% dplyr::rename(geneID = gene_id)
  }

  final_go_df <- final_go_df %>%
    dplyr::select(
      dplyr::any_of(c(
        "Analysis_Group", "GO_Name", "ID", "GO_Definition",
        "Count", "GeneRatio", "BgRatio", "pvalue",
        "p.adjust", "qvalue", "geneID"
      ))
    )

  # Save locally
  if (!dir.exists(results_dir)) dir.create(results_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  out_path <- file.path(results_dir, "go_anno_cluster_results.csv")
  write.csv(final_go_df, out_path, row.names = FALSE)

  message("GO Analysis complete. File saved to: ", out_path)
} else {
  message("No significant GO enrichment found for these clusters.")
}

# Force R to point 'select' and 'filter' back to dplyr

filter <- dplyr::filter

message("Namespace reset: 'select' and 'filter' now point back to dplyr.")
```

```{r !!!go-enrichment-semantic-terminology-sep-trees}
# ==========================================
# 1. Define Variables & Library Loading
# ==========================================
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(AnnotationDbi)
library(GO.db)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(enrichplot)
library(ggplot2)

qtable <- 0.3 # q threshold for out table
ptable <- 0.05 # p threshold for out table
clust_thresh <- 0.25 # cluster membership threshold
target_db <- "GO_bak"

# ==========================================
# 2. Define Background & Map Genes to GO Terms
# ==========================================
raw_universe_genes <- rownames(dds)

t2g <- anno_operon_clean %>%
  filter(Gene %in% raw_universe_genes) %>%
  dplyr::select(!!sym(target_db), Gene) %>%
  drop_na(!!sym(target_db)) %>%
  separate_rows(!!sym(target_db), sep = ", ") %>%
  filter(!!sym(target_db) != "" & !!sym(target_db) != "NA") %>%
  rename(term_id = !!sym(target_db), gene_id = Gene) %>%
  distinct()

universe_vector <- unique(t2g$gene_id)

# --- NEW CRITICAL FIX: Build Global TERM2NAME Mapping ---
# This ensures treeplot gets names instead of GO:XXXXXX codes
message("Building GO ID to Term Name mapping table...")
all_go_ids_in_universe <- unique(t2g$term_id)

t2n <- AnnotationDbi::select(
  x       = GO.db,
  keys    = all_go_ids_in_universe,
  columns = c("GOID", "TERM"),
  keytype = "GOID"
) %>%
  dplyr::rename(term_id = GOID, term_name = TERM) %>%
  distinct()
# --------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare cluster inputs
cluster_input <- df_final_clusters %>%
  filter(is_driver == "High-Confidence" & Gene %in% universe_vector)

all_clusters <- sort(unique(cluster_input$cluster))
enrich_list <- list()

message("Starting GO Enrichment for ", length(all_clusters), " clusters...")

# ==========================================
# 3. Enrichment Loop & Visualization Generation
# ==========================================
for (clust_id in all_clusters) {
  current_genes <- cluster_input %>%
    filter(cluster == clust_id) %>%
    pull(Gene)

  ego <- enricher(
    gene         = current_genes,
    universe     = universe_vector,
    TERM2GENE    = t2g,
    TERM2NAME    = t2n, # <-- Passed directly into engine so plots are labeled
    pvalueCutoff = ptable,
    qvalueCutoff = qtable,
    minGSSize    = 2
  )

  # Check if there are valid results before continuing
  if (!is.null(ego) && nrow(as.data.frame(ego)) > 0) {
    # Force 'BP' ontology so enrichplot doesn't choke on custom/generic objects
    ego@ontology <- "BP"

    # Use Jaccard Coefficient (JC) based on overlap matrix of custom genes
    ego_sim <- pairwise_termsim(ego, method = "JC", semData = NULL)

    # Generate treeplot if there are enough terms to cluster (at least 2)
    if (nrow(as.data.frame(ego)) > 1) {
      # Suppress internal lifecycle package warnings cleanly
      suppressWarnings({
        p_tree <- treeplot(ego_sim, showCategory = 40) +
          labs(
            title = paste0("Cluster ", clust_id, " GO Tree (Top 40 Terms)"),
            subtitle = "Terms grouped by semantic similarity based on gene overlap"
          )

        # Ensure results directory exists before saving plots
        if (!dir.exists(results_dir)) dir.create(results_dir, recursive = TRUE)

        ggsave(
          filename = file.path(results_dir, paste0("cluster_", clust_id, "_treeplot.png")),
          plot = p_tree,
          width = 15, # Slightly wider to comfortably fit full term names
          height = 11,
          dpi = 300
        )
      })
    }

    # Save text results to master dataframe list
    enrich_list[[as.character(clust_id)]] <- as.data.frame(ego) %>%
      mutate(Analysis_Group = paste0("Cluster_", clust_id))
  } else {
    message("No significant GO enrichment found passing thresholds for Cluster ", clust_id)
  }
}

# ==========================================
# 4. Lookup Metadata, Merge, and Save Table
# ==========================================
if (length(enrich_list) > 0) {
  all_go_res <- bind_rows(enrich_list)
  unique_go_ids <- unique(all_go_res$ID)

  message("Mapping extra metadata for ", length(unique_go_ids), " unique GO terms...")

  go_metadata_df <- AnnotationDbi::select(
    x       = GO.db,
    keys    = unique_go_ids,
    columns = c("GOID", "TERM", "DEFINITION"),
    keytype = "GOID"
  ) %>%
    dplyr::rename(ID = GOID, GO_Name = TERM, GO_Definition = DEFINITION)

  # Merge metadata with results (keeping columns consistent)
  final_go_df <- all_go_res %>%
    dplyr::left_join(go_metadata_df, by = "ID")

  # Standardize gene column naming conventions across variations of clusterProfiler
  if (!"geneID" %in% colnames(final_go_df) & "gene_id" %in% colnames(final_go_df)) {
    final_go_df <- final_go_df %>% dplyr::rename(geneID = gene_id)
  }

  final_go_df <- final_go_df %>%
    dplyr::select(
      dplyr::any_of(c(
        "Analysis_Group", "GO_Name", "ID", "GO_Definition",
        "Count", "GeneRatio", "BgRatio", "pvalue",
        "p.adjust", "qvalue", "geneID"
      ))
    )

  # Save local CSV
  if (!dir.exists(results_dir)) dir.create(results_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  out_path <- file.path(results_dir, "go_anno_cluster_results.csv")
  write.csv(final_go_df, out_path, row.names = FALSE)

  message("GO Analysis complete. File and plots successfully saved with descriptive text names.")
} else {
  message("Process finished: No significant GO enrichment across any clusters.")
}

# ==========================================
# 5. Reset Namespace
# ==========================================
select <- dplyr::select
filter <- dplyr::filter

message("Namespace reset: 'select' and 'filter' point back to dplyr.")
```


```{r go-comparison-fixed}
# ==========================================
# 1. Setup Data Structures
# ==========================================
library(dplyr)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(enrichplot)
library(ggplot2)

# Make sure cluster IDs are clean characters or factors
cluster_input <- cluster_input %>%
  mutate(cluster = as.character(cluster))

all_clusters <- sort(unique(cluster_input$cluster))
individual_enrichments <- list()

message("Running individual clusters to build a comparative merge object...")

# ==========================================
# 2. Run Individual Enrichments Safely
# ==========================================
for (clust_id in all_clusters) {
  current_genes <- cluster_input %>%
    filter(cluster == clust_id) %>%
    pull(Gene)

  ego <- enricher(
    gene         = current_genes,
    universe     = universe_vector,
    TERM2GENE    = t2g,
    TERM2NAME    = t2n,
    pvalueCutoff = ptable,
    qvalueCutoff = qtable,
    minGSSize    = 2
  )

  # Only keep it if it has valid significant terms
  if (!is.null(ego) && nrow(as.data.frame(ego)) > 0) {
    ego@ontology <- "BP" # Ensure internal mapping works safely
    individual_enrichments[[paste0("Cluster_", clust_id)]] <- ego
  }
}

# ==========================================
# 3. Merge Results and Build Comparative Visualization
# ==========================================
if (length(individual_enrichments) > 0) {
  message("Merging ", length(individual_enrichments), " functional profiles...")

  # clusterProfiler's built-in tool to natively stitch individual objects together
  merged_comp_ego <- merge_result(individual_enrichments)

  # Calculate global semantic similarity across the comparative database
  merged_comp_ego <- pairwise_termsim(merged_comp_ego, method = "JC", semData = NULL)

  # Generate the side-by-side comparison plot
  # showCategory = 5 takes the top 5 functional modules per cluster to display across all
  suppressWarnings({
    p_compare <- dotplot(merged_comp_ego, x = "Cluster", showCategory = 5) +
      labs(
        title = "Functional Mapping Across Analysis Groups",
        subtitle = "Collapsed modules compared side-by-side via merged clusters"
      ) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vinterv = 0.5),
        axis.text.y = element_text(fontsize = 9)
      )

    # Save comparison plot
    if (!dir.exists(results_dir)) dir.create(results_dir, recursive = TRUE)
    ggsave(
      filename = file.path(results_dir, "all_clusters_compared_dotplot.png"),
      plot = p_compare,
      width = 14,
      height = 12,
      dpi = 300
    )
  })

  message("Master comparative dotplot saved successfully.")
} else {
  message("No valid comparative groups to merge.")
}
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# 1. INITIALIZATION & BACKGROUND SETUP
# ==============================================================================
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(AnnotationDbi)
library(GO.db)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(enrichplot)
library(ggplot2)

qtable <- 0.3 # q threshold for output filtering
ptable <- 0.05 # p threshold for output filtering
clust_thresh <- 0.25 # cluster membership threshold
target_db <- "GO_bak"

# Define background universe from detectable genes
raw_universe_genes <- rownames(dds)

# Map background genes to custom GO terms
t2g <- anno_operon_clean %>%
  filter(Gene %in% raw_universe_genes) %>%
  dplyr::select(!!sym(target_db), Gene) %>%
  drop_na(!!sym(target_db)) %>%
  separate_rows(!!sym(target_db), sep = ", ") %>%
  filter(!!sym(target_db) != "" & !!sym(target_db) != "NA") %>%
  rename(term_id = !!sym(target_db), gene_id = Gene) %>%
  distinct()

universe_vector <- unique(t2g$gene_id)

# Build a comprehensive TERM2NAME mapping table from GO.db
message("Building global GO term-to-name lookup table...")
all_go_ids_in_universe <- unique(t2g$term_id)

t2n <- AnnotationDbi::select(
  x       = GO.db,
  keys    = all_go_ids_in_universe,
  columns = c("GOID", "TERM"),
  keytype = "GOID"
) %>%
  dplyr::rename(term_id = GOID, term_name = TERM) %>%
  distinct()

# Filter target driver genes present in our background universe
cluster_input <- df_final_clusters %>%
  filter(is_driver == "High-Confidence" & Gene %in% universe_vector)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. COMPARE FIRST: RUN MULTI-GROUP ENRICHMENT UNIFIED
# ==============================================================================
message("Splitting genes into cluster list and initiating compareCluster...")

# Format clusters into a clean, named list of gene vectors to avoid splitting errors
gene_list_by_cluster <- split(cluster_input$Gene, cluster_input$cluster)

# Run comparative enrichment across all groups concurrently
comp_ego <- compareCluster(
  geneClusters = gene_list_by_cluster,
  fun          = "enricher",
  universe     = universe_vector,
  TERM2GENE    = t2g,
  TERM2NAME    = t2n,
  pvalueCutoff = ptable,
  qvalueCutoff = qtable
)

# --- CORRECTED ONTOLOGY PATCH ---
# Use attr() since 'ontology' is a core metadata attribute for compareClusterResult
attr(comp_ego, "ontology") <- "BP"

# ==============================================================================
# 3. INTERSECT: COMPUTE THE SHARED NETWORK SIMILARITY MATRIX
# ==============================================================================
message("Calculating global semantic similarity matrix via Jaccard Coefficient...")

# Calculate overlapping gene similarities across the whole uncollapsed dataset
comp_ego_sim <- pairwise_termsim(comp_ego, method = "JC", semData = NULL)

# ==============================================================================
# 4. COLLAPSE & RENDER ONCE: VISUALIZATION GENERATION
# ==============================================================================
message("Collapsing redundant terms and plotting master comparative dotplot...")

suppressWarnings({
  # showCategory = 5 groups hundreds of terms into modules, displaying the top 5 per cluster
  p_compare <- dotplot(comp_ego_sim, x = "Cluster", showCategory = 5) +
    labs(
      title = "Functional Mapping Across Analysis Groups",
      subtitle = "Redundant terms collapsed dynamically; top modules compared side-by-side",
      x = "Analysis Group (Cluster)",
      y = "Enriched Functional Module"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
      axis.text.y = element_text(fontsize = 9),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)
    )

  # Ensure the results folder exists and write the comparative plot
  if (!dir.exists(results_dir)) dir.create(results_dir, recursive = TRUE)

  out_plot_path <- file.path(results_dir, "all_clusters_compared_dotplot.png")
  ggsave(
    filename = out_plot_path,
    plot = p_compare,
    width = 15,
    height = 12,
    dpi = 300
  )
})

message("Success! Master comparative bubble plot saved to: ", out_plot_path)

# ==============================================================================
# 5. ENVIRONMENT / NAMESPACE RESET
# ==============================================================================
select <- dplyr::select
filter <- dplyr::filter
message("Namespace reset: 'select' and 'filter' point back to dplyr.")
```

```{r}
high_level_tiers <- data.frame(
  Parent_ID = c(
    # --- Carbon & General Metabolism ---
    "GO:0005975", # Carbohydrate metabolic process
    "GO:0006629", # Lipid metabolic process
    "GO:0044237", # Cellular metabolic process (General)
    "GO:0019752", # Carboxylic acid metabolic process (Toxicant breakdown)
    "GO:0055114", # Oxidation-reduction process (Energy / P450s)

    # --- Specialized Metabolism & Amino Acids ---
    "GO:0009081", # Branched-chain amino acid metabolic process (Leu/Ile/Val)

    # --- Stress, Resistance, Transport, & Membrane ---
    "GO:0006950", # Response to stress
    "GO:0046677", # Response to antibiotic (Antibiotic resistance/defense)
    "GO:0006810", # Transport (Efflux pumps / Transporters)
    "GO:0016044", # Cellular membrane organization (Membrane Remodeling)
    "GO:0044038", # Cell wall macromolecule metabolic process

    # --- Phage & Mobile Genetic Elements ---
    "GO:0019058", # Viral life cycle / Virion assembly (Phage-associated terms)

    # --- Morphology & Development ---
    "GO:0030435", # Sporulation / Endospores
    "GO:0043903", # Dormancy Regulation

    # --- Growth & Reproduction (Housekeeping to isolate/ignore) ---
    "GO:0040007", # Growth
    "GO:0000278", # Cell division
    "GO:0008135" # Translation / Ribosomes
  ),
  Parent_Name = c(
    "Carbohydrate Metabolism",
    "Lipid Metabolism",
    "General Cellular Metabolism",
    "Organic Acid/Toxicant Metabolism",
    "Oxidation-Reduction Energy",
    "BCAA Metabolism (Leu/Ile/Val)",
    "Stress Response",
    "Antibiotic Response/Resistance",
    "Transport & Efflux",
    "Membrane Remodeling",
    "Cell Wall Remodeling",
    "Phage-associated/Viral Process",
    "Sporulation & Endospores",
    "Dormancy Regulation",
    "Growth (Housekeeping)",
    "Cell Division (Housekeeping)",
    "Translation/Ribosomes (Housekeeping)"
  )
)

# ==========================================
# 3. EXTRACT GRAPH ANCESTORS (SPECIES AGNOSTIC)
# ==========================================
# Extract unique GO IDs from your specific non-model dataframe
unique_go_ids <- unique(final_go_df$ID)

# Get the full core graph for Biological Processes
ancestor_list <- as.list(GOBPANCESTOR)

# Filter down graph to only include your 500 enriched terms
filtered_ancestors <- ancestor_list[names(ancestor_list) %in% unique_go_ids]

# ==========================================
# 4. MULTI-ASSIGNMENT MAPPING LOGIC
# ==========================================
# Map your specific terms to ALL applicable high-level parents they belong to
mapping_list <- lapply(names(filtered_ancestors), function(go_id) {
  parents <- filtered_ancestors[[go_id]]

  # Check which defined high-level targets match this GO ID's ancestors
  matched_parents <- high_level_tiers$Parent_ID[high_level_tiers$Parent_ID %in% parents]

  if (length(matched_parents) > 0) {
    # Returns a row for EVERY matched high-level parent (allows cross-assignment)
    return(data.frame(ID = go_id, Parent_ID = matched_parents))
  } else {
    return(data.frame(ID = go_id, Parent_ID = "Other/Specific"))
  }
})

# Combine results into a clean lookup dataframe
go_to_parent_map <- do.call(rbind, mapping_list) %>%
  left_join(high_level_tiers, by = "Parent_ID") %>%
  mutate(Parent_Name = ifelse(is.na(Parent_Name), "Other/Specific", Parent_Name))
```

```{r}
library(GO.db)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# ==========================================
# 1. DEFINE A COMPREHENSIVE MULTI-ONTOLOGY TIER LIST
# ==========================================
# This combines BP, MF, and CC terms tailored to your toxicant/energy data
high_level_tiers <- data.frame(
  Parent_ID = c(
    # --- Biological Processes (BP) ---
    "GO:0019752", # Carboxylic/Organic acid metabolic process (Toxicant breakdown)
    "GO:0006091", # Generation of precursor metabolites and energy
    "GO:0006119", # Oxidative phosphorylation (Energy generation)
    "GO:0055114", # Oxidation-reduction process
    "GO:0005975", # Carbohydrate metabolic process
    "GO:0006629", # Lipid metabolic process
    "GO:0009081", # BCAA metabolic process (Leu/Ile/Val)
    "GO:0006950", # Response to stress
    "GO:0046677", # Response to antibiotic / Resistance
    "GO:0006810", # Transport / Efflux
    "GO:0016044", # Cellular membrane organization (Remodeling)
    "GO:0030435", # Sporulation / Endospores
    "GO:0019058", # Viral life cycle (Phage-associated)
    "GO:0006399", # tRNA metabolic process (Translation housekeeping)
    "GO:0040007", # Growth / Cell Division

    # --- Molecular Functions (MF) ---
    "GO:0001882", # Nucleoside binding (Includes ATP/GTP binding)
    "GO:0005524", # ATP binding
    "GO:0005525", # GTP binding
    "GO:0004812", # Aminoacyl-tRNA ligase activity (Translation machinery)
    "GO:0003824", # Catalytic activity (General enzyme upregulation)
    "GO:0022857", # Transporter activity

    # --- Cellular Components (CC) ---
    "GO:0005829", # Cytosol
    "GO:0005886" # Plasma membrane
  ),
  Parent_Name = c(
    # BP Names
    "Organic Acid/Toxicant Metabolism",
    "Precursor Metabolite/Energy Gen",
    "Oxidative Phosphorylation",
    "Oxidation-Reduction Energy",
    "Carbohydrate Metabolism",
    "Lipid Metabolism",
    "BCAA Metabolism (Leu/Ile/Val)",
    "Stress Response",
    "Antibiotic Response/Resistance",
    "Transport & Efflux",
    "Membrane Remodeling",
    "Sporulation & Endospores",
    "Phage-associated/Viral Process",
    "tRNA Metabolism (Housekeeping)",
    "Growth & Division (Housekeeping)",

    # MF Names
    "Nucleoside/Purine Binding",
    "ATP Binding (Energetics)",
    "GTP Binding (Signaling)",
    "Aminoacyl-tRNA Ligase (Housekeeping)",
    "Enzymatic Catalytic Activity",
    "Transporter Activity",

    # CC Names
    "Cytosol (Cellular Location)",
    "Plasma Membrane (Cellular Location)"
  )
)

# ==========================================
# 2. DYNAMIC MULTI-ONTOLOGY ANCESTOR LOOKUP
# ==========================================
unique_go_ids <- unique(final_go_df$ID)

# Convert fundamental environments to lists once
bp_ancestors <- as.list(GOBPANCESTOR)
mf_ancestors <- as.list(GOMFANCESTOR)
cc_ancestors <- as.list(GOCCANCESTOR)

mapping_list <- lapply(unique_go_ids, function(go_id) {
  # 1. Determine which ontology branch the term belongs to and get ancestors
  parents <- NULL
  if (go_id %in% names(bp_ancestors)) {
    parents <- bp_ancestors[[go_id]]
  } else if (go_id %in% names(mf_ancestors)) {
    parents <- mf_ancestors[[go_id]]
  } else if (go_id %in% names(cc_ancestors)) {
    parents <- cc_ancestors[[go_id]]
  }

  # Include the term itself as a "parent" just in case it IS one of our high-level targets
  all_nodes <- c(go_id, parents)

  # 2. Match against our curated target lists
  matched_parents <- high_level_tiers$Parent_ID[high_level_tiers$Parent_ID %in% all_nodes]

  if (length(matched_parents) > 0) {
    return(data.frame(ID = go_id, Parent_ID = matched_parents))
  } else {
    # If it genuinely doesn't match our targets, send to fallback
    return(data.frame(ID = go_id, Parent_ID = "Other/Specific"))
  }
})

# Combine into a clean lookup dataframe
go_to_parent_map <- do.call(rbind, mapping_list) %>%
  left_join(high_level_tiers, by = "Parent_ID") %>%
  mutate(Parent_Name = ifelse(is.na(Parent_Name), "Other/Specific", Parent_Name))
```

```{r}
    "GO:0001882", # Nucleoside binding

    "GO:0004812" # Aminoacyl-tRNA ligase activity
  ),
  Parent_Name = c(
    # BP Labels
    "Organic Acid/Toxicant Metabolism",
    "Precursor Metabolite/Energy Gen",
    "Oxidative Phosphorylation",
    "Oxidation-Reduction Energy",
    "Carbohydrate Metabolism",
    "Lipid Metabolism",
    "BCAA Metabolism (Leu/Ile/Val)",

    "Hydrolase (Substrate Cleavage)",

    "Lyase (Carbon Slicing)",

    "Transcription Factor Activity",
    "DNA Binding",
    "RNA Binding (Temporal Control)",

# ==========================================
# 3. GRAPH ANCESTOR LOOKUP (BP & MF Only)
# ==========================================
unique_go_ids <- unique(final_go_df$ID)

bp_ancestors <- as.list(GOBPANCESTOR)
mf_ancestors <- as.list(GOMFANCESTOR)

mapping_list <- lapply(unique_go_ids, function(go_id) {
  parents <- NULL
  if (go_id %in% names(bp_ancestors)) {
    parents <- bp_ancestors[[go_id]]
  } else if (go_id %in% names(mf_ancestors)) {
    parents <- mf_ancestors[[go_id]]
  }

  all_nodes <- c(go_id, parents)
  matched_parents <- high_level_tiers$Parent_ID[high_level_tiers$Parent_ID %in% all_nodes]

  if (length(matched_parents) > 0) {
    return(data.frame(ID = go_id, Parent_ID = matched_parents))
  } else {
    return(data.frame(ID = go_id, Parent_ID = "Other/Specific"))
  }
})

go_to_parent_map <- do.call(rbind, mapping_list) %>%
  left_join(high_level_tiers, by = "Parent_ID") %>%
  mutate(Parent_Name = ifelse(is.na(Parent_Name), "Other/Specific", Parent_Name))

# ==========================================
# 4. MERGE, ONTOLOGY SEPARATION, & AGGREGATE
# ==========================================
summarized_go_df <- final_go_df %>%
  left_join(go_to_parent_map, by = "ID", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  # Assign high-level Ontology classes based on the Parent Name groups
  mutate(Ontology = case_when(
    Parent_Name %in% c(
      "Oxidoreductase (Detox/Energy)", "Hydrolase (Substrate Cleavage)",
      "Transferase (Conjugation/Detox)", "Lyase (Carbon Slicing)",
      "Isomerase (Metabolic Shuffling)", "Transcription Factor Activity",
      "DNA Binding", "RNA Binding (Temporal Control)", "Transporter Activity",
      "ATP Binding", "Nucleoside/Purine Binding", "Kinase/Signaling Cascades",
      "Aminoacyl-tRNA Ligase"
    ) ~ "Molecular Function",
    TRUE ~ "Biological Process"
  )) %>%
  # Filter out CC terms entirely if any snuck in through fallback paths
  filter(Parent_Name != "Other/Specific") %>%
  group_by(Analysis_Group, Parent_Name, Ontology) %>%
  summarize(
    Best_p.adjust = min(p.adjust, na.rm = TRUE),
    Term_Count = n(),
    Total_Gene_Count = sum(Count, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(neg_log_p = -log10(Best_p.adjust))
```

It looks like I lost clusters 5 and 6 during original analysis - possibly because:
- Cluster 6 has a lot of core metabolic genes (versions of which are also present in other clusters, due to the nature of core metabolism)
- Cluster 5 appears to be primarily early physiological response, which be more scattered and involved small gene clusters

Try to rescue

```{r}
# ==========================================
# 1. PARAMETERS & UNIVERSE SETUP
# ==========================================
target_db <- "GO_bak"
clust_thresh <- 0.25
results_dir <- "/mnt/work-drive/kira/deseq2New/final-split"

# Define background from detectable genes
raw_universe_genes <- rownames(dds)

# Surgical split to map genes to GO terms
# Surgical split to map genes to GO terms
t2g <- anno_operon_clean %>%
  filter(Gene %in% raw_universe_genes) %>%
  # Use dplyr:: explicitly here
  dplyr::select(!!sym(target_db), Gene) %>%
  drop_na(!!sym(target_db)) %>%
  separate_rows(!!sym(target_db), sep = ", ") %>%
  filter(!!sym(target_db) != "" & !!sym(target_db) != "NA") %>%
  rename(term_id = !!sym(target_db), gene_id = Gene) %>%
  distinct()
universe_vector <- unique(t2g$gene_id)

# ==========================================
# 2. RUN GO ENRICHMENT LOOP (RESCUE VERSION)
# ==========================================
cluster_input <- df_final_clusters %>%
  filter(membership_score >= clust_thresh & Gene %in% universe_vector)

all_clusters <- sort(unique(cluster_input$cluster))
enrich_list <- list()

message("Starting GO Enrichment for ", length(all_clusters), " clusters...")

for (clust_id in all_clusters) {
  current_genes <- cluster_input %>%
    filter(cluster == clust_id) %>%
    pull(Gene)

  ego <- enricher(
    gene         = current_genes,
    universe     = universe_vector,
    TERM2GENE    = t2g,
    # --- RELAXED PARAMETERS TO RESCUE DROPOUT CLUSTERS ---
    pvalueCutoff = 0.20, # Raised from 0.05 to pull in core metabolism and small signaling suites
    qvalueCutoff = 0.4, # Raised to let borderline temporal trends pass through
    minGSSize    = 2
  )

  if (!is.null(ego) && nrow(ego@result) > 0) {
    # Extract ALL results from the object, not just the strictly filtered slots
    res_df <- as.data.frame(ego)

    if (nrow(res_df) > 0) {
      enrich_list[[as.character(clust_id)]] <- res_df %>%
        mutate(Analysis_Group = paste0("Cluster_", clust_id))
      message("  -> Cluster ", clust_id, " successfully generated ", nrow(res_df), " enrichment terms.")
    }
  } else {
    message("  !! Cluster ", clust_id, " returned 0 terms even with relaxed parameters.")
  }
}
# ==========================================
# 3. LOCAL METADATA LOOKUP
# ==========================================
library(GO.db)

if (length(enrich_list) > 0) {
  all_go_res <- bind_rows(enrich_list)
  unique_go_ids <- unique(all_go_res$ID)

  message("Mapping metadata for ", length(unique_go_ids), " unique GO terms...")

  # Explicitly use AnnotationDbi for the database query
  go_metadata_df <- AnnotationDbi::select(
    x       = GO.db,
    keys    = unique_go_ids,
    columns = c("GOID", "TERM", "DEFINITION"),
    keytype = "GOID"
  ) %>%
    dplyr::rename(ID = GOID, GO_Name = TERM, GO_Definition = DEFINITION)

  # ==========================================
  # 4. FINAL MERGE & CLEANUP
  # ==========================================

  final_go_df <- all_go_res %>%
    dplyr::left_join(go_metadata_df, by = "ID")

  # Safety Check: Print column names to console so you can see what survived the join
  # print(colnames(final_go_df))

  # Use 'any_of' to prevent the "object not found" error if a column is missing
  final_go_df <- final_go_df %>%
    dplyr::select(
      dplyr::any_of(c(
        "GO_Name", "ID", "GO_Definition", "Analysis_Group",
        "Count", "GeneRatio", "BgRatio", "pvalue",
        "p.adjust", "qvalue", "geneID"
      ))
    )

  # Save locally
  if (!dir.exists(results_dir)) dir.create(results_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  out_path <- file.path(results_dir, "go_anno_cluster_results.csv")
  write.csv(final_go_df, out_path, row.names = FALSE)

  message("GO Analysis complete. File saved to: ", out_path)
} else {
  message("No significant GO enrichment found for these clusters.")
}

# RESET NAMESPACE,
# Force R to point 'select' and 'filter' back to dplyr
select <- dplyr::select
filter <- dplyr::filter

message("Namespace reset: 'select' and 'filter' now point back to dplyr.")
```

```{r}
# ==========================================
# 2. MAP TOTAL GENOMICS WEIGHT TO SLIM NODES (NO P-VALUE FILTER)
# ==========================================
library(GO.db)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Extract full universe mapping from your original clean t2g object
# This maps EVERY gene to its specific GO terms
all_genes_go <- t2g %>% rename(Gene = gene_id, ID = term_id)

unique_go_ids <- unique(all_genes_go$ID)
bp_ancestors <- as.list(GOBPANCESTOR)
mf_ancestors <- as.list(GOMFANCESTOR)

# Build a structural map of which GO terms belong to which Slim parent
message("Structuring GOslim Graph Tree...")
slim_mapping_list <- lapply(unique_go_ids, function(go_id) {
  parents <- NULL
  if (go_id %in% names(bp_ancestors)) {
    parents <- bp_ancestors[[go_id]]
  } else if (go_id %in% names(mf_ancestors)) parents <- mf_ancestors[[go_id]]

  all_nodes <- c(go_id, parents)
  matched_slims <- goslim_tiers$Parent_ID[goslim_tiers$Parent_ID %in% all_nodes]

  if (length(matched_slims) > 0) {
    return(data.frame(ID = go_id, Parent_ID = matched_slims))
  } else {
    return(NULL)
  }
})

go_to_slim_map <- do.call(rbind, slim_mapping_list) %>%
  left_join(goslim_tiers, by = "Parent_ID")

# ==========================================
# 3. INTERSECT WITH FUZZY CLUSTER MEMBERSHIP
# ==========================================
# Use ALL cluster genes matching your membership threshold (unfiltered by enrichment)
cluster_genes_raw <- df_final_clusters %>%
  filter(membership_score >= clust_thresh) %>%
  mutate(Analysis_Group = paste0("Cluster_", cluster))

# Link genes -> GO Terms -> Slim Tiers
goslim_counts <- cluster_genes_raw %>%
  inner_join(all_genes_go, by = "Gene", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  inner_join(go_to_slim_map, by = "ID", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  # Determine Ontology panel
  mutate(Ontology = case_when(
    Parent_ID %in% c(
      "GO:0003824", "GO:0016491", "GO:0016787", "GO:0016740",
      "GO:0016829", "GO:0016853", "GO:0016874", "GO:0003700",
      "GO:0003677", "GO:0003723", "GO:0005524", "GO:0022857"
    ) ~ "Molecular Function",
    TRUE ~ "Biological Process"
  )) %>%
  # Group and count the structural density
  group_by(Analysis_Group, Slim_Name, Ontology) %>%
  summarize(Unique_Gene_Count = n_distinct(Gene), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Normalize by cluster size so large clusters don't visually distort small ones
  group_by(Analysis_Group) %>%
  mutate(Percentage_of_Cluster_Genes = (Unique_Gene_Count / sum(Unique_Gene_Count)) * 100)

# ==========================================
# 4. PLOT STRUCTURAL GOSLIM DISTRIBUTION
# ==========================================
ggplot(goslim_counts, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = Slim_Name)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Percentage_of_Cluster_Genes, color = Percentage_of_Cluster_Genes)) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "deepskyblue", high = "navy") +
  facet_grid(Ontology ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 270, face = "bold", size = 11),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = "white"),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray95")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Structural Functional Fingerprint Across Bacterial Clusters",
    subtitle = "True GOslim Topological Distribution (No Statistical Threshold Filtering)",
    x = "Fuzzy Analysis Group",
    y = "Standardized GOslim Branches",
    size = "% of Total Cluster Weight",
    color = "% Density"
  )
```

# !!! ELIM

```{r}
# BiocManager::install("topGO")
library(topGO)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

# Prepare a clean, named list mapping Genes to GO terms for topGO
gene_2_go_list <- split(t2g$term_id, t2g$gene_id)

# Identify all available clusters from your fuzzy clustering input
all_cluster_ids <- sort(unique(df_final_clusters$cluster))

# Custom wrapper to run Elim for a single ontology branch
run_tiered_ontology <- function(current_cluster, ontology_branch) {
  # Get genes belonging to the current cluster
  cluster_genes <- df_final_clusters %>%
    filter(cluster == current_cluster & is_driver == "High-Confidence") %>%
    #        filter(cluster == current_cluster & membership_score >= clust_thresh) %>%
    pull(Gene)

  # Create the binary factor vector topGO expects (1 = in cluster, 0 = background)
  selector_vector <- as.integer(universe_vector %in% cluster_genes)
  names(selector_vector) <- universe_vector
  selector_vector <- factor(selector_vector)

  # Initialize the structural topGO data object
  go_data_obj <- new("topGOdata",
    ontology = ontology_branch,
    allGenes = selector_vector,
    annot = annFUN.gene2GO,
    gene2GO = gene_2_go_list
  )

  # Execute the TRUE tiered Elim algorithm
  elim_result <- runTest(go_data_obj, algorithm = "elim", statistic = "fisher")

  # Extract the top non-redundant terms
  raw_table <- GenTable(go_data_obj,
    Elim_p = elim_result,
    orderBy = "Elim_p",
    topNodes = 40,
    numChar = 1000
  )

  # Format and clean the output metadata
  raw_table %>%
    mutate(
      Analysis_Group = paste0("Cluster_", current_cluster),
      Ontology = ifelse(ontology_branch == "BP", "Biological Process", "Molecular Function"),
      # Clean character p-values (e.g., "< 1e-30") to numeric values
      p.adjust = as.numeric(gsub("< ", "", Elim_p))
    ) %>%
    filter(p.adjust <= 0.05) %>% # Keep terms that survived decorrelation
    dplyr::rename(ID = GO.ID, GO_Name = Term) %>%
    dplyr::select(Analysis_Group, ID, GO_Name, Ontology, p.adjust, Significant)
}
```

```{r}
message("Running global structural Elim decorrelation...")

compiled_elim_results <- map_dfr(all_cluster_ids, function(clust) {
  message("  Processing Cluster ", clust, "...")

  # Safe execution block to gracefully handle empty/flat branches
  bp_res <- tryCatch(run_tiered_ontology(clust, "BP"), error = function(e) NULL)
  mf_res <- tryCatch(run_tiered_ontology(clust, "MF"), error = function(e) NULL)

  bind_rows(bp_res, mf_res)
})

# Quick validation check to confirm cluster presence
print(table(compiled_elim_results$Analysis_Group))
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. FILTER & PREPARE DATA
# ==============================================================================
bp_plot_data <- compiled_elim_results %>%
  filter(Ontology == "Biological Process") %>%
  mutate(neg_log_p = -log10(p.adjust)) %>%
  # Select top terms per cluster to keep the vertical axis manageable
  group_by(Analysis_Group) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = neg_log_p, n = 8, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

# ==============================================================================
# 2. MANUALLY CALCULATE HIERARCHICAL CLUSTERING FOR AXES
# ==============================================================================
# Step A: Pivot to a wide matrix layout (Rows = GO Terms, Columns = Clusters)
# We cluster based on the -log10(p) profile across groups.
wide_matrix_df <- bp_plot_data %>%
  dplyr::select(GO_Name, Analysis_Group, neg_log_p) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Analysis_Group, values_from = neg_log_p, values_fill = 0)

# Convert to standard numeric matrix format
clust_matrix <- as.matrix(wide_matrix_df[, -1])
rownames(clust_matrix) <- wide_matrix_df$GO_Name

# Step B: Perform Hierarchical Clustering on ROWS (GO Terms)
row_dist <- dist(clust_matrix, method = "euclidean")
row_hc <- hclust(row_dist, method = "complete")
go_term_order <- rownames(clust_matrix)[row_hc$order]

# Step C: Perform Hierarchical Clustering on COLUMNS (Analysis Groups / Clusters)
# (Only cluster columns if you have 3 or more groups)
if (ncol(clust_matrix) >= 3) {
  col_dist <- dist(t(clust_matrix), method = "euclidean")
  col_hc <- hclust(col_dist, method = "complete")
  analysis_group_order <- colnames(clust_matrix)[col_hc$order]
} else {
  analysis_group_order <- sort(unique(bp_plot_data$Analysis_Group))
}

# ==============================================================================
# 3. APPLY CLUSTERED ORDER BACK TO PLOT DATA
# ==============================================================================
bp_plot_clustered_data <- bp_plot_data %>%
  mutate(
    GO_Name        = factor(GO_Name, levels = go_term_order),
    Analysis_Group = factor(Analysis_Group, levels = analysis_group_order)
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 4. RENDER CLUSTERED BUBBLE PLOT
# ==============================================================================
bp_plot <- ggplot(bp_plot_clustered_data, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = GO_Name)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Significant, color = neg_log_p)) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "steelblue1", high = "purple", name = "-log10(p)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray95"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Hierarchically Clustered BP Functional Landscape",
    subtitle = "Decorrelated Macro-Phenotypes & Temporal Pathways via Elim",
    x = "Hierarchically Ordered Cluster Waves",
    y = "Clustered Biological Process Terms",
    size = "Gene Count"
  )

# Render plot in device
bp_plot

# Save file with plenty of canvas space
if (!dir.exists(results_dir)) dir.create(results_dir, recursive = TRUE)
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(results_dir, "elim_landscape_biological_process_rescue_hier_n8.pdf"),
  plot = bp_plot,
  width = 9,
  height = 12,
  units = "in"
)
```

Still impossible to parse. let's use heirarchical clustering.
Reshape Elim results into a wide matrix (Terms $\times$ Clusters), calculates a distance metric based on how terms co-occur across your time-course waves, and uses hclust() to define the natural functional modules.
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)

# 1. Pivot the Elim results into a binary presence/absence matrix (1 = significant, 0 = not)
matrix_prep <- compiled_elim_results %>%
  mutate(Present = 1) %>%
  distinct(GO_Name, Analysis_Group, Ontology, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(GO_Name, Ontology),
    names_from = Analysis_Group,
    values_from = Present,
    values_fill = 0
  )

# 2. Isolate the numeric matrix profiles for distance calculation
profile_matrix <- matrix_prep %>%
  select(-GO_Name, -Ontology) %>%
  as.matrix()
rownames(profile_matrix) <- matrix_prep$GO_Name

# 3. Compute distances and run Hierarchical Clustering on the GO Terms
# Binary (Jaccard-like) distance is ideal for presence/absence profiling
term_distances <- dist(profile_matrix, method = "binary")
term_clustering <- hclust(term_distances, method = "complete")

# 4. Extract the optimal, structured sorting order from the dendrogram
ordered_terms <- term_clustering$labels[term_clustering$order]

# 5. Re-align the original long data frame to match this clean hierarchical order
ordered_plot_df <- compiled_elim_results %>%
  mutate(
    neg_log_p = -log10(p.adjust),
    # Force the GO_Name factor levels to strictly follow the clustering order
    GO_Name = factor(GO_Name, levels = ordered_terms)
  )
```

```{r}
bp_heatmap <- ggplot(bp_heatmap_df, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = GO_Name)) +

  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, name = "-log10(p)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 7), # Small, clean grid text
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Hierarchical Functional Modules: Biological Processes",
    subtitle = "Terms Grouped Structurally by Shared Wave Profiles (Elim Data)",
    x = "Temporal Cluster Wave",
    y = "Clustered Biological Processes"
```
