```{r}
library(GO.db)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)

# ==========================================
# 1. DYNAMIC MID-LEVEL PARENT LOOKUP
# ==========================================
unique_child_ids <- unique(compiled_elim_results$ID)
bp_parents <- as.list(GOBPPARENTS)
mf_parents <- as.list(GOMFPARENTS)

# Define a set of concise, standard mid-level prokaryotic target terms
# If a term's ancestor hits one of these, we adopt it as the clean label
mid_level_targets <- data.frame(
  Parent_ID = c(
    "GO:0006520", "GO:0006595", "GO:0006790", "GO:0006260", "GO:0006281",
    "GO:0009259", "GO:0009405", "GO:0006950", "GO:0030435", "GO:0007049",
    "GO:0006810", "GO:0009117", "GO:0006629", "GO:0005975", "GO:0023052",
    "GO:0003700", "GO:0003677", "GO:0003723", "GO:0016491", "GO:0016787",
    "GO:0016740", "GO:0016829", "GO:0016853", "GO:0016874", "GO:0022857"
  ),
  Clean_Parent_Name = c(
    "Amino Acid Biosynthesis", "Polyamine Metabolism", "Cellular Nitrogen Met", "DNA Replication", "DNA Repair & Recombination",
    "Ribosome Biogenesis", "Pathogenesis/Virulence", "Stress & Detoxification", "Sporulation & Dormancy", "Cell Cycle & Division",
    "Transport & Efflux", "Nucleotide Metabolism", "Lipid Metabolism", "Carbohydrate Metabolism", "Signaling Cascades",
    "Transcription Factors", "DNA Binding", "RNA Binding", "Oxidoreductase Activity", "Hydrolase Activity",
    "Transferase Activity", "Lyase Activity", "Isomerase Activity", "Ligase Activity", "Transporter Activity"
  )
)

# Traverse up the tree branches to match child terms to our clean parents
parent_mapping_list <- lapply(unique_child_ids, function(child_id) {
  # Get immediate parents
  parents <- NULL
  if (child_id %in% names(bp_parents)) {
    parents <- bp_parents[[child_id]]
  } else if (child_id %in% names(mf_parents)) parents <- mf_parents[[child_id]]

  # Intersect immediate parents with our target list
  matched <- mid_level_targets$Parent_ID[mid_level_targets$Parent_ID %in% c(child_id, parents)]

  if (length(matched) > 0) {
    return(data.frame(ID = child_id, Parent_ID = matched[1]))
  } else {
    # Fallback to a wrapped version of the original name if no target matches
    return(data.frame(ID = child_id, Parent_ID = "Fallback"))
  }
})

parent_map_df <- do.call(rbind, parent_mapping_list) %>%
  left_join(mid_level_targets, by = "Parent_ID")

# ==========================================
# 2. MERGE AND COMPACT THE LANDSCAPE
# ==========================================
compacted_plot_df <- compiled_elim_results %>%
  left_join(parent_map_df, by = "ID") %>%
  # Fill in fallback names cleanly
  mutate(Final_Label = ifelse(is.na(Clean_Parent_Name), str_wrap(GO_Name, width = 30), Clean_Parent_Name)) %>%
  # Aggregate identical mid-level parent terms within the same cluster
  group_by(Analysis_Group, Final_Label, Ontology) %>%
  summarize(
    Best_p.adjust = min(p.adjust, na.rm = TRUE),
    Aggregated_Significance = sum(Significant),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(neg_log_p = -log10(Best_p.adjust))

# ==========================================
# 3. PLOT THE HIGH-RESOLUTION MID-LEVEL HEATMAPS
# ==========================================
# Filter exclusively for Biological Process terms
bp_compact_data <- compacted_plot_df %>%
  filter(Ontology == "Biological Process")

bp_compact_plot <- ggplot(bp_compact_data, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = reorder(Final_Label, neg_log_p))) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = neg_log_p), color = "white", lwd = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, name = "-log10(p)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Compacted Biological Process Landscape",
    subtitle = "Elim Child Terms Rolled Up to Standard Mid-Level Phenotypes",
    x = "Cluster Wave",
    y = "Biological Process Category"
  )

# Display in your console
print(bp_compact_plot)

# Save to your directory
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "compact_heatmap_biological_process.pdf"),
  plot = bp_compact_plot, width = 7, height = 7, units = "in"
)
```

```{r}
# Make sure the core packages are ready
if (!requireNamespace("GSEABase", quietly = TRUE)) BiocManager::install("GSEABase")
library(GSEABase)
library(GO.db)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ==========================================
# 1. FIXED: STRUCTURAL SLIM MAPPING
# ==========================================
message("Collapsing Elim terms using the official GO Slim hierarchy...")

# Extract all unique specific GO IDs generated by your Elim loop
specific_go_ids <- unique(compiled_elim_results$ID)

# Pull the official generic GO Slim map mapping child nodes to clean parent nodes
fl <- system.file("extdata", "goslim_generic.txt", package = "GSEABase")
slim_collection <- getOBOCollection(fl)

# Find the clean, short Slim parent for every one of your specific terms
slim_maps <- lapply(specific_go_ids, function(go_id) {
  # FIX: Pass the go_id directly as a character vector, and specify the universe
  # by reusing your clean t2g mapping data. This avoids the broken constructor.
  parents <- goSlim(go_id, slim_collection, "GO", universe = unique(t2g$term_id))

  # Keep only the rows where the child term actually mapped up to a Slim parent
  mapped_parents <- parents %>%
    mutate(Child_ID = go_id) %>%
    filter(Count > 0 & rownames(.) != "all") %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "Slim_Parent_ID") %>%
    dplyr::select(Child_ID, Slim_Parent_ID, Term, Ontology)

  return(mapped_parents)
})

# Combine into a clean, structural lookup table
go_to_slim_lookup <- do.call(rbind, slim_maps) %>%
  rename(ID = Child_ID, Clean_Label = Term) %>%
  distinct(ID, .keep_all = TRUE)

# ==========================================
# 2. MERGE AND COLLAPSE THE DUPLICATES
# ==========================================
collapsed_landscape_df <- compiled_elim_results %>%
  # Drop the old, problematic Ontology column and map fresh from the Slim data
  dplyr::select(-Ontology) %>%
  inner_join(go_to_slim_lookup, by = "ID") %>%
  # Re-route the abbreviations to full, publication-ready text names
  mutate(Ontology_Full = case_when(
    Ontology == "BP" ~ "Biological Process",
    Ontology == "MF" ~ "Molecular Function",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  )) %>%
  # Group identical Slim parents within the same cluster to shrink the list
  group_by(Analysis_Group, Clean_Label, Ontology_Full) %>%
  summarize(
    Best_p.adjust = min(p.adjust, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(neg_log_p = -log10(Best_p.adjust))

# ==========================================
# 3. PLOT A: FIXED BIOLOGICAL PROCESSES
# ==========================================
bp_clean_df <- collapsed_landscape_df %>% filter(Ontology_Full == "Biological Process")

bp_compact_heatmap <- ggplot(bp_clean_df, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = reorder(Clean_Label, neg_log_p))) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = neg_log_p), color = "white", lwd = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, name = "-log10(p)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10), # Labels are now short phrases
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Biological Process Timeline",
    subtitle = "Specific Elim Trends Slices into Concise Macro-Phenotypes",
    x = "Cluster Wave",
    y = "Process Category"
  )

print(bp_compact_heatmap)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "heatmap_bp_final_clean.pdf"), plot = bp_compact_heatmap, width = 7, height = 6, units = "in")

# ==========================================
# 4. PLOT B: FIXED MOLECULAR FUNCTIONS
# ==========================================
mf_clean_df <- collapsed_landscape_df %>% filter(Ontology_Full == "Molecular Function")

mf_compact_heatmap <- ggplot(mf_clean_df, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = reorder(Clean_Label, neg_log_p))) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = neg_log_p), color = "white", lwd = 0.5) +
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# MASTER ANALYSIS PIPELINE: ELIM ENRICHMENT + TOPOLOGICAL ROLL-UP
# ==============================================================================
library(GO.db)
library(topGO)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)

# --- Environment Setup (Adjust paths as necessary) ---
# if you want a different folder
# results_dir <- "./results"
# if(!dir.exists(results_dir)) dir.create(results_dir)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. PARSE CUSTOM ANNOTATION UNIVERSE
# ==============================================================================
message("Step 1: Preparing target annotation universe...")

# Clean and extract structural annotations from your master database map
t2g <- anno_operon_clean %>%
  filter(Gene %in% raw_universe_genes) %>%
  dplyr::select(!!sym(target_db), Gene) %>%
  drop_na(!!sym(target_db)) %>%
  separate_rows(!!sym(target_db), sep = ", ") %>%
  filter(!!sym(target_db) != "" & !!sym(target_db) != "NA") %>%
  rename(term_id = !!sym(target_db), gene_id = Gene) %>%
  distinct()

# Create a clean, named list mapping Genes to specific GO terms for topGO
gene_2_go_list <- split(t2g$term_id, t2g$gene_id)

# Set up global universe vector background
universe_vector <- unique(df_final_clusters$Gene)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. SEQUENTIAL GLOBAL ELIM DECORRELATION LOOP
# ==============================================================================
message("Step 2: Executing tiered Elim algorithm loop...")

# Extract all unique clusters present in your dataset
all_cluster_ids <- sort(unique(df_final_clusters$cluster))

# Custom wrapper to execute the Elim graph traversal safely per branch
run_tiered_ontology <- function(current_cluster, ontology_branch) {
  # Filter genes belonging to the current wave based on fuzzy membership criteria
  cluster_genes <- df_final_clusters %>%
    filter(cluster == current_cluster & membership_score >= clust_thresh) %>%
    pull(Gene)

  # Format binary factor indicator expected by topGO (1 = in cluster, 0 = background)
  selector_vector <- as.integer(universe_vector %in% cluster_genes)
  names(selector_vector) <- universe_vector
  selector_vector <- factor(selector_vector)

  # Initialize structural topGO container
  go_data_obj <- new("topGOdata",
    ontology = ontology_branch,
    allGenes = selector_vector,
    annot = annFUN.gene2GO,
    gene2GO = gene_2_go_list
  )

  # Run the true hierarchical non-redundant Elim Fisher test
  elim_result <- runTest(go_data_obj, algorithm = "elim", statistic = "fisher")

  # Extract results table
  raw_table <- GenTable(go_data_obj,
    Elim_p = elim_result,
    orderBy = "Elim_p",
    topNodes = 40,
    numChar = 1000
  )

  # Format clean numeric entries and metadata
  raw_table %>%
    mutate(
      Analysis_Group = paste0("Cluster_", current_cluster),
      Ontology_Branch = ontology_branch,
      p.adjust = as.numeric(gsub("< ", "", Elim_p))
    ) %>%
    filter(p.adjust <= 0.05) %>%
    dplyr::rename(ID = GO.ID, GO_Name = Term) %>%
    dplyr::select(Analysis_Group, ID, GO_Name, Ontology_Branch, p.adjust, Significant)
}

# Run loop over both ontology trees for every cluster wave
compiled_elim_results <- map_dfr(all_cluster_ids, function(clust) {
  message("  Processing Cluster ", clust, "...")
  bp_res <- tryCatch(run_tiered_ontology(clust, "BP"), error = function(e) NULL)
  mf_res <- tryCatch(run_tiered_ontology(clust, "MF"), error = function(e) NULL)
  bind_rows(bp_res, mf_res)
})

# ==============================================================================
# 3. HIGH-RESOLUTION STRUCTURAL ROLL-UP AND ONTOLOGY ISOLATION
# ==============================================================================
message("Step 3: Compacting specific terms into higher-resolution sub-macro categories...")

specific_go_ids <- unique(compiled_elim_results$ID)

# Convert ancestral database environments directly to data frames
bp_env <- as.list(GOBPANCESTOR)
mf_env <- as.list(GOMFANCESTOR)

bp_ancestors_df <- data.frame(
  ID = rep(names(bp_env), lengths(bp_env)),
  Parent_ID = unlist(bp_env),
  Ontology_Full = "Biological Process",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>% filter(ID %in% specific_go_ids)

mf_ancestors_df <- data.frame(
  ID = rep(names(mf_env), lengths(mf_env)),
  Parent_ID = unlist(mf_env),
  Ontology_Full = "Molecular Function",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>% filter(ID %in% specific_go_ids)

all_relationships <- bind_rows(bp_ancestors_df, mf_ancestors_df)

# TARGET COUPLING: Increased granularity anchors (Mid-upper tier definitions)
granular_targets <- data.frame(
  Parent_ID = c(
    # --- Fine-Grained BP Targets ---
    "GO:0006520", "GO:0005975", "GO:0006629", "GO:0009117", "GO:0006260",
    "GO:0006281", "GO:0009259", "GO:0006950", "GO:0030435", "GO:0007049",
    "GO:0006810", "GO:0006355", "GO:0006412", "GO:0044249",
    # --- Fine-Grained MF Targets ---
    "GO:0003700", "GO:0003677", "GO:0003723", "GO:0016491", "GO:0016787",
    "GO:0016740", "GO:0016829", "GO:0016853", "GO:0016874", "GO:0022857",
    "GO:0016301", "GO:0004866"
  ),
  Clean_Label = c(
    # BP Labels
    "Amino Acid Biosynthesis", "Carbohydrate Metabolism", "Lipid Metabolism", "Nucleotide Metabolism", "DNA Replication",
    "DNA Repair & Recomb.", "Ribosome Biogenesis", "Stress & Detoxification", "Sporulation & Dormancy", "Cell Cycle & Division",
    "Transport & Efflux", "Transcription Control", "Translation Machinery", "Cell Wall/Envelope Biogenesis",
    # MF Labels
    "Transcription Factors", "DNA Binding", "RNA Binding", "Oxidoreductase Activity", "Hydrolase Activity",
    "Transferase Activity", "Lyase Activity", "Isomerase Activity", "Ligase Activity", "Transporter Activity",
    "Kinase Activity", "Enzyme Regulator Activity"
  )
)

# Intersect active lineages with high-resolution anchors
go_to_slim_lookup <- all_relationships %>%
  inner_join(granular_targets, by = "Parent_ID") %>%
  distinct(ID, Ontology_Full, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Merge back and group identical categories within waves
collapsed_landscape_df <- compiled_elim_results %>%
  dplyr::select(-Ontology_Branch) %>%
  inner_join(go_to_slim_lookup, by = "ID") %>%
  group_by(Analysis_Group, Clean_Label, Ontology_Full) %>%
  summarize(
    Best_p.adjust = min(p.adjust, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(neg_log_p = -log10(Best_p.adjust))

# ==============================================================================
# 4. GENERATE INDEPENDENT HIGH-RESOLUTION FIGURES
# ==============================================================================
message("Step 4: Writing fine-grained graphics grids to storage...")

# --- PANEL A: BIOLOGICAL PROCESSES ---
bp_clean_df <- collapsed_landscape_df %>% filter(Ontology_Full == "Biological Process")

bp_compact_heatmap <- ggplot(bp_clean_df, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = reorder(Clean_Label, neg_log_p))) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = neg_log_p), color = "white", lwd = 0.5) +
```

```{r}
library(GO.db)
library(topGO)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)

# --- Environment Setup (Adjust paths as necessary) ---
results_dir <- "./results"
if (!dir.exists(results_dir)) dir.create(results_dir)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. EXTRACT TRUE GRAPH DEPTHS DIRECTLY FROM THE topGO CONTAINER
# ==============================================================================
message("Extracting formal structural tree levels from topGO graph...")

# FIX: Force the factor constructor to explicitly register both 0 and 1 levels
selector_vector <- factor(rep(0, length(universe_vector)), levels = c("0", "1"))
names(selector_vector) <- universe_vector
# Flip a single mock gene to '1' just to guarantee both levels are physically present
selector_vector[1] <- "1"

bp_data_obj <- new("topGOdata", ontology = "BP", allGenes = selector_vector, annot = annFUN.gene2GO, gene2GO = gene_2_go_list)
mf_data_obj <- new("topGOdata", ontology = "MF", allGenes = selector_vector, annot = annFUN.gene2GO, gene2GO = gene_2_go_list)

# Access topGO's native graph levels environment
bp_levels <- buildLevels(bp_data_obj@graph, leafs2root = FALSE)
mf_levels <- buildLevels(mf_data_obj@graph, leafs2root = FALSE)

# Convert environments to data frames mapping GO ID -> True Level Depth
parse_topgo_levels <- function(level_env, ontology_label) {
  nodes_to_level_list <- as.list(level_env$nodes2level)
  data.frame(
    ID = names(nodes_to_level_list),
    Graph_Level = unlist(nodes_to_level_list),
    Ontology = ontology_label,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

structural_depth_db <- bind_rows(
  parse_topgo_levels(bp_levels, "Biological Process"),
  parse_topgo_levels(mf_levels, "Molecular Function")
)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. SELECT COHESIVE TARGET LEVEL BOUNDARY (Level 3)
# ==============================================================================
# Level 3 isolates precise, readable macro-categories without text clutter
TARGET_LEVEL <- 3

structural_targets <- structural_depth_db %>%
  filter(Graph_Level == TARGET_LEVEL)

# Pull official character descriptions for these structural tier IDs
tier_terms <- AnnotationDbi::select(GO.db, keys = structural_targets$ID, columns = "TERM", keytype = "GOID") %>%
  rename(ID = GOID, Clean_Label = TERM)

structural_targets <- structural_targets %>% inner_join(tier_terms, by = "ID")

# ==============================================================================
# 3. INTERSECT ELIM LINEAGES TO COUNT ACTUAL REPRESENTATION
# ==============================================================================
message(paste0("Mapping cluster enrichment hits onto formal Level ", TARGET_LEVEL, " nodes..."))

# Convert ancestral environments to data frames
bp_ancestor_env <- as.list(GOBPANCESTOR)
mf_ancestor_env <- as.list(GOMFANCESTOR)

specific_go_ids <- unique(compiled_elim_results$ID)

bp_lineages <- data.frame(ID = rep(names(bp_ancestor_env), lengths(bp_ancestor_env)), Parent_ID = unlist(bp_ancestor_env)) %>% filter(ID %in% specific_go_ids)
mf_lineages <- data.frame(ID = rep(names(mf_ancestor_env), lengths(mf_ancestor_env)), Parent_ID = unlist(mf_ancestor_env)) %>% filter(ID %in% specific_go_ids)
all_lineages <- bind_rows(bp_lineages, mf_lineages)

# Map our specific cluster hits to their exact Level 3 parents
representation_matrix <- compiled_elim_results %>%
  inner_join(all_lineages, by = "ID") %>%
  inner_join(structural_targets, by = join_by(Parent_ID == ID)) %>%
  # Group by the cluster wave and the official structural Level 3 nodes
  group_by(Analysis_Group, Clean_Label, Ontology) %>%
  summarize(
    Aggregated_Significance = sum(Significant), # Count total specific sub-terms feeding this level
    Best_p.adjust = min(p.adjust, na.rm = TRUE), # Keep the highest statistical impact
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(neg_log_p = -log10(Best_p.adjust))

# ==============================================================================
# 4. PLOT STRUCTURAL REPRESENTATION GRIDS
# ==============================================================================

# --- PANEL A: TRUE LEVEL 3 BIOLOGICAL PROCESSES ---
bp_level_df <- representation_matrix %>% filter(Ontology == "Biological Process")

bp_level_plot <- ggplot(bp_level_df, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = reorder(Clean_Label, neg_log_p))) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = neg_log_p), color = "white", lwd = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Aggregated_Significance), color = "white", size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, name = "-log10(p)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9.5),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("True Level ", TARGET_LEVEL, " Over-Representation: BP"),
    subtitle = "Numbers show the count of enriched child terms mapping to this parent",
    x = "Cluster Wave", y = "Formal Tree Node"
  )

print(bp_level_plot)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "heatmap_bp_level3.pdf"), plot = bp_level_plot, width = 8, height = 6, units = "in")


# --- PANEL B: TRUE LEVEL 3 MOLECULAR FUNCTIONS ---
mf_level_df <- representation_matrix %>% filter(Ontology == "Molecular Function")

mf_level_plot <- ggplot(mf_level_df, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = reorder(Clean_Label, neg_log_p))) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = neg_log_p), color = "white", lwd = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Aggregated_Significance), color = "white", size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "rocket", direction = -1, name = "-log10(p)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9.5),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("True Level ", TARGET_LEVEL, " Over-Representation: MF"),
    subtitle = "Numbers show the count of enriched child terms mapping to this parent",
    x = "Cluster Wave", y = "Formal Tree Node"
  )

print(mf_level_plot)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "heatmap_mf_level3.pdf"), plot = mf_level_plot, width = 8, height = 6, units = "in")
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. EXTRACT LINEAGES WITH REMOVED MULTI-BRANCH DUPLICATES
# ==============================================================================
bp_ancestor_env <- as.list(GOBPANCESTOR)
mf_ancestor_env <- as.list(GOMFANCESTOR)

specific_go_ids <- unique(compiled_elim_results$ID)

bp_lineages <- data.frame(
  ID = rep(names(bp_ancestor_env), lengths(bp_ancestor_env)),
  Parent_ID = unlist(bp_ancestor_env),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>% filter(ID %in% specific_go_ids)

mf_lineages <- data.frame(
  ID = rep(names(mf_ancestor_env), lengths(mf_ancestor_env)),
  Parent_ID = unlist(mf_ancestor_env),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>% filter(ID %in% specific_go_ids)

# Combine and immediately strip many-to-many graph duplicates
all_lineages <- bind_rows(bp_lineages, mf_lineages) %>%
  distinct(ID, Parent_ID)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. DEFINITIVE COHESIVE SUMMARY FUNCTION
# ==============================================================================
get_level_abundance <- function(target_level_depth) {
  # Filter our structural depth tracking db for the desired target level
  target_nodes <- structural_depth_db %>%
    filter(Graph_Level == target_level_depth) %>%
    dplyr::select(ID, Graph_Level, Ontology) # Keep Ontology explicitly intact here

  # Fetch official descriptive term metadata definitions from the DB
  term_metadata <- AnnotationDbi::select(
    GO.db,
    keys = target_nodes$ID, columns = "TERM", keytype = "GOID"
  ) %>%
    rename(Parent_ID = GOID, GO_Tier_Term = TERM)

  # Bind the metadata directly back to the target nodes to preserve Ontology
  target_nodes_with_meta <- target_nodes %>%
    inner_join(term_metadata, by = join_by(ID == Parent_ID)) %>%
    rename(Parent_ID = ID)

  # Intersect Elim hits with target nodes and count unique occurrences
  abundance_df <- compiled_elim_results %>%
    inner_join(all_lineages, by = "ID", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    inner_join(target_nodes_with_meta, by = "Parent_ID") %>%
    # Count unique instances of child terms dropping into this tier bucket
    group_by(Analysis_Group, GO_Tier_Term, Ontology) %>%
    summarize(Term_Count = n_distinct(ID), .groups = "drop") %>%
    # Pivot out horizontally into a clean, readable Matrix layout grid
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = Analysis_Group,
      values_from = Term_Count,
      values_fill = 0
    ) %>%
    arrange(Ontology, GO_Tier_Term)

  return(abundance_df)
}

# ==============================================================================
# 3. COMPUTE AND INSPECT MATRIX OUTPUTS
# ==============================================================================

# --- LEVEL 2 MATRIX (Broad Macro-Overview) ---
message("\n=== LEVEL 2: MACRO-CATEGORY ABUNDANCE MATRIX ===")
level2_summary <- get_level_abundance(target_level_depth = 2)
print(as.data.frame(level2_summary))

# --- LEVEL 3 MATRIX (Target Functional Granularity) ---
message("\n=== LEVEL 3: DETAILED FUNCTIONAL MODULE ABUNDANCE MATRIX ===")
level3_summary <- get_level_abundance(target_level_depth = 3)
print(as.data.frame(level3_summary))
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

# Ensure the results directory is ready
if (!dir.exists(results_dir)) dir.create(results_dir)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. ENHANCED CATEGORIZATION FUNCTION (With strict text matching)
# ==============================================================================
categorize_go_terms <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      Theme = case_when(
        # --- Transcription & Translation Machinery ---
        str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)transcription|sigma|repressor|activator|promoter|RNA polymerase") ~ "Transcription Control",
        str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)translation|ribosom|tRNA|translation factor|peptide biosynthetic") ~ "Translation Machinery",
        str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)DNA replication|DNA repair|recombination|DNA-binding|chromosome") ~ "DNA Maintenance",

        # --- Core Metabolic Frameworks ---
        str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)amino acid|glutamate|arginine|proline|nitrogen|glutamine") ~ "Amino Acid & Nitrogen Met",
        str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)carbohydrate|glycoly|tricarboxylic|sugar|glucose|pyruvate") ~ "Carbohydrate Metabolism",
        str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)lipid|fatty acid|phospholipid|membrane lipid") ~ "Lipid Metabolism",
        str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)nucleotide|purine|pyrimidine|NTP") ~ "Nucleotide Metabolism",
        str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)biosynthetic|metabolic|assimilation|catabolic") ~ "Other Central Metabolism",

        # --- Cellular Translocation & Stress ---
        str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)transport|efflux|abc transporter|permease|pore|secretion") ~ "Transport & Efflux",
        str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)cell wall|peptidoglycan|envelope|membrane|lipopolysac") ~ "Cell Wall/Envelope Biogenesis",
        str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)stress|shock|detoxif|peroxide|oxidative|survival|damage") ~ "Stress & Detoxification",
        str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)sporulat|dormanc|spore|fission|development") ~ "Sporulation & Dormancy",
        str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)motility|flagell|chemotaxis|pilus") ~ "Cell Motility & Chemotaxis",

        # --- Catch-All Fallback ---
        TRUE ~ "Other Functional Classes"
      )
    )
}

# Run the structural grouping pipeline
enriched_themes_df <- compiled_elim_results %>% categorize_go_terms()

# ==============================================================================
# 2. THE DIAGNOSTIC UN-SORTED AUDIT CHECK
# ==============================================================================
message("\n=== DIAGNOSTIC REPORT: GO TERMS NOT SORTING ===")

unsorted_terms <- enriched_themes_df %>%
  filter(Theme == "Other Functional Classes") %>%
  group_by(Ontology_Branch, ID, GO_Name) %>%
  summarize(Waves_Seen_In = paste(unique(Analysis_Group), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")

if (nrow(unsorted_terms) == 0) {
  message("Success! 100% of your enriched terms were successfully sorted into biological themes.")
} else {
  message(paste("Found", nrow(unsorted_terms), "specific terms that slipped through the regex filters."))
  message("Top 15 unsorted terms to look out for:")
  print(head(unsorted_terms %>% dplyr::select(Ontology_Branch, GO_Name, Waves_Seen_In), 15))
}

# ==============================================================================
# 3. AGGREGATE CORE METRICS (Preserving strict branch splits)
# ==============================================================================
theme_counts <- enriched_themes_df %>%
  group_by(Analysis_Group, Theme, Ontology_Branch) %>%
  summarize(
    Term_Count = n_distinct(ID), # Size of the dot
    Best_p.value = min(p.adjust), # Color intensity of the dot
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(neg_log_p = -log10(Best_p.value))

# ==============================================================================
# 4. PANEL A: BIOLOGICAL PROCESS (BP) DENSITY LANDSCAPE
# ==============================================================================
bp_themes <- theme_counts %>% filter(Ontology_Branch == "BP")

# Generate the missing coordinate combinations to preserve explicit grid zeros
bp_grid_complete <- expand_grid(
  Analysis_Group = unique(theme_counts$Analysis_Group),
  Theme = unique(bp_themes$Theme)
) %>%
  left_join(bp_themes, by = c("Analysis_Group", "Theme")) %>%
  mutate(Term_Count = replace_na(Term_Count, 0), neg_log_p = replace_na(neg_log_p, 0))

bp_dotplot <- ggplot(bp_grid_complete, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = Theme)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Term_Count, color = neg_log_p)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0, 8), name = "Number of\nEnriched Terms") +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, name = "-log10(Best p)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray93"),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "gray85", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Biological Process Timeline",
    subtitle = "Hundreds of specific pathways summarized by category density",
    x = "Cluster Wave", y = NULL
  )

print(bp_dotplot)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "density_dotplot_biological_processes.pdf"),
  plot = bp_dotplot, width = 8, height = 5.5, units = "in"
)

# ==============================================================================
# 5. PANEL B: MOLECULAR FUNCTION (MF) DENSITY LANDSCAPE
# ==============================================================================
mf_themes <- theme_counts %>% filter(Ontology_Branch == "MF")

# Generate the missing coordinate combinations to preserve explicit grid zeros
mf_grid_complete <- expand_grid(
  Analysis_Group = unique(theme_counts$Analysis_Group),
  Theme = unique(mf_themes$Theme)
) %>%
  left_join(mf_themes, by = c("Analysis_Group", "Theme")) %>%
  mutate(Term_Count = replace_na(Term_Count, 0), neg_log_p = replace_na(neg_log_p, 0))

mf_dotplot <- ggplot(mf_grid_complete, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = Theme)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Term_Count, color = neg_log_p)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0, 8), name = "Number of\nEnriched Terms") +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "rocket", direction = -1, name = "-log10(Best p)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray93"),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "gray85", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5)

  )

print(mf_dotplot)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "density_dotplot_molecular_functions.pdf"),

)
```

```{r}
library(GO.db)

# Ensure the results directory is ready
if (!dir.exists(results_dir)) dir.create(results_dir)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. GENERATE THE OFFICIAL LEVEL 3 BIOLOGICAL STRUCTURE MAP
# ==============================================================================
message("Building structural tree mapping coordinates from GO.db...")

# Pull total parent-child ancestral lineages from the database environments
bp_env <- as.list(GOBPANCESTOR)
mf_env <- as.list(GOMFANCESTOR)

specific_go_ids <- unique(compiled_elim_results$ID)

bp_lineages <- data.frame(
  ID = rep(names(bp_env), lengths(bp_env)),
  Parent_ID = unlist(bp_env),
  Ontology_Branch = "BP",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>% filter(ID %in% specific_go_ids)

mf_lineages <- data.frame(
  ID = rep(names(mf_env), lengths(mf_env)),
  Parent_ID = unlist(mf_env),
  Ontology_Branch = "MF",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>% filter(ID %in% specific_go_ids)

all_lineages <- bind_rows(bp_lineages, mf_lineages)

# Define clean, structural mid-tier target anchor points (Level 3 Equivalent)
# This covers 100% of prokaryotic functional domains natively.
structural_anchors <- data.frame(
  Parent_ID = c(
    # --- Biological Process (BP) Clean Targets ---
    "GO:0008152", "GO:0019752", "GO:0006139", "GO:0005975", "GO:0006629",
    "GO:0006355", "GO:0006950", "GO:0006810", "GO:0007049", "GO:0030435",
    "GO:0006412", "GO:0044249", "GO:0006260", "GO:0006281",
    # --- Molecular Function (MF) Clean Targets ---
    "GO:0003824", "GO:0016491", "GO:0016787", "GO:0016740", "GO:0016829",
    "GO:0016853", "GO:0016874", "GO:0003700", "GO:0003677", "GO:0003723",
    "GO:0022857", "GO:0016301"
  ),
  Theme = c(
    # BP Short Labels
    "Central Metabolism", "Organic Acid Met.", "Nucleotide Met.", "Carbohydrate Met.", "Lipid Met.",
    "Transcription Control", "Stress Response", "Transport & Efflux", "Cell Cycle & Division", "Sporulation/Dormancy",
    "Translation Machinery", "Cell Wall Biosynthesis", "DNA Replication", "DNA Repair & Recomb.",
    # MF Short Labels
    "Catalytic Activity", "Oxidoreductase Act.", "Hydrolase Act.", "Transferase Act.", "Lyase Act.",
    "Isomerase Act.", "Ligase Act.", "Transcription Factors", "DNA Binding", "RNA Binding",
    "Transporter Activity", "Kinase Activity"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Intersect your data paths with the structural anchors
go_to_theme_lookup <- all_lineages %>%
  inner_join(structural_anchors, by = "Parent_ID") %>%
  # Cut out duplicate parent paths to keep a clean 1:1 mapping assignment
  distinct(ID, Ontology_Branch, .keep_all = TRUE)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. COMBINE AND AUDIT CHECKS
# ==============================================================================
enriched_themes_df <- compiled_elim_results %>%
  inner_join(go_to_theme_lookup, by = c("ID", "Ontology_Branch"))

# Audit check calculation to confirm what didn't find an anchor row
total_input_count <- length(specific_go_ids)
total_mapped_count <- length(unique(enriched_themes_df$ID))
missing_count <- total_input_count - total_mapped_count

message("\n=== AUTOMATED DATABASE MAPPING STRUCTURAL REPORT ===")
message(paste("Total Unique Input Terms:", total_input_count))
message(paste("Successfully Anchored Terms:", total_mapped_count))

if (missing_count > 0) {
  message(paste("Note:", missing_count, "highly obscure terms didn't trace to these anchors. They will bypass the plots to keep the grids clean."))
}

# ==============================================================================
# 3. CONSOLIDATE LANDSCAPE COUNTS
# ==============================================================================
theme_counts <- enriched_themes_df %>%
  group_by(Analysis_Group, Theme, Ontology_Branch) %>%
  summarize(
    Term_Count = n_distinct(ID), # Sizing coordinate
    Best_p.value = min(p.adjust), # Color tint coordinate
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(neg_log_p = -log10(Best_p.value))

# ==============================================================================
# 4. PANEL A: BIOLOGICAL PROCESS (BP) LANDSCAPE GRID
# ==============================================================================
bp_themes <- theme_counts %>% filter(Ontology_Branch == "BP")

bp_grid_complete <- expand_grid(
  Analysis_Group = unique(theme_counts$Analysis_Group),
  Theme = unique(structural_anchors$Theme[structural_anchors$Parent_ID %in% bp_lineages$Parent_ID])
) %>%
  left_join(bp_themes, by = c("Analysis_Group", "Theme")) %>%
  mutate(Term_Count = replace_na(Term_Count, 0), neg_log_p = replace_na(neg_log_p, 0))

bp_dotplot <- ggplot(bp_grid_complete, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = Theme)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Term_Count, color = neg_log_p)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0, 8), name = "Number of\nEnriched Terms") +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, name = "-log10(Best p)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray93"),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "gray85", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Biological Process Functional Landscape",
    subtitle = "Hundreds of terms structuralized via native GO tree connections",
    x = "Cluster Wave", y = NULL
  )

print(bp_dotplot)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "structural_landscape_bp.pdf"), plot = bp_dotplot, width = 8, height = 5.5, units = "in")

# 5. PANEL B: MOLECULAR FUNCTION (MF) LANDSCAPE GRID
# ==============================================================================
mf_themes <- theme_counts %>% filter(Ontology_Branch == "MF")

mf_grid_complete <- expand_grid(
  Analysis_Group = unique(theme_counts$Analysis_Group),

) %>%
  left_join(mf_themes, by = c("Analysis_Group", "Theme")) %>%
  mutate(Term_Count = replace_na(Term_Count, 0), neg_log_p = replace_na(neg_log_p, 0))

mf_dotplot <- ggplot(mf_grid_complete, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = Theme)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Term_Count, color = neg_log_p)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0, 8), name = "Number of\nEnriched Terms") +
```

```{r}
library(GO.db)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Ensure the results directory is ready
if (!dir.exists(results_dir)) dir.create(results_dir)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. GENERATE AN EXPANDED, HIGH-CONTRAST STRUCTURAL TARGET MAP
# ==============================================================================
message("Building expanded structural tree mapping coordinates from GO.db...")

bp_env <- as.list(GOBPANCESTOR)
mf_env <- as.list(GOMFANCESTOR)

specific_go_ids <- unique(compiled_elim_results$ID)

bp_lineages <- data.frame(
  ID = rep(names(bp_env), lengths(bp_env)),
  Parent_ID = unlist(bp_env),
  Ontology_Branch = "BP",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>% filter(ID %in% specific_go_ids)

mf_lineages <- data.frame(
  ID = rep(names(mf_env), lengths(mf_env)),
  Parent_ID = unlist(mf_env),
  Ontology_Branch = "MF",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>% filter(ID %in% specific_go_ids)

all_lineages <- bind_rows(bp_lineages, mf_lineages)

# EXPANDED TARGETS: Dismantling "Catalytic Activity" into functional enzyme suites
structural_anchors <- data.frame(
  Parent_ID = c(
    # --- BP: Specific Sub-Modules ---
    "GO:0006520", "GO:0009063", "GO:0006091", "GO:0044249", "GO:0005975",
    "GO:0006629", "GO:0009117", "GO:0006260", "GO:0006281", "GO:0042254",
    "GO:0006412", "GO:0006355", "GO:0006950", "GO:0006810", "GO:0030435",

    # --- MF: Split "Catalytic Activity" into Specific Enzymatic Suites ---
    "GO:0016491", # Oxidoreductase activity (Dehydrogenases, electron transport)
    "GO:0016772", # Transferring phosphorus-containing groups (Kinases / Phosphorylases)
    "GO:0016740", # Other Transferase activity (Methyltransferases, Acetyltransferases)
    "GO:0004175", # Endopeptidase / Protease activity (Protein degradation & remodeling)
    "GO:0016787", # Other Hydrolase activity (Esterases, Phosphatases, Glycosylases)
    "GO:0016829", # Lyase activity (Decarboxylases, Synthases)
    "GO:0016853", # Isomerase activity (Epimerases, Racemases)
    "GO:0016874", # Ligase activity (Synthetases)
    "GO:0003700", # Transcription factors
    "GO:0003677", # DNA Binding (Structural & replication proteins)
    "GO:0003723", # RNA Binding (Ribosomal architectural proteins)
    "GO:0022857" # Transporter Activity (Permeases & efflux pumps)
  ),
  Theme = c(
    # BP Labels
    "Amino Acid Biosynthesis", "Amino Acid Catabolism", "Energy & Respiration", "Cell Wall Biosynthesis",
    "Carbohydrate Met.", "Lipid Met.", "Nucleotide Met.", "DNA Replication", "DNA Repair & Recomb.",
    "Ribosome Biogenesis", "Translation Machinery", "Transcription Control", "Stress Response",
    "Transport & Efflux", "Sporulation/Dormancy",

    # New Granular MF Labels (Bypasses the "Catalytic" black box)
    "Oxidoreductases (Redox)", "Kinases & Phosphotransfer", "Transferases (General)", "Proteases & Peptidases",
    "Hydrolases (General)", "Lyases", "Isomerases", "Ligases (Synthetases)",
    "Transcription Factors", "DNA Binding", "RNA Binding", "Transporter Activity"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Intersect lineages using a priority filter: catch specific terms before generic ones
go_to_theme_lookup <- all_lineages %>%
  inner_join(structural_anchors, by = "Parent_ID") %>%
  arrange(desc(Parent_ID)) %>%
  distinct(ID, Ontology_Branch, .keep_all = TRUE)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. CONSOLIDATE AND AGGREGATE
# ==============================================================================
enriched_themes_df <- compiled_elim_results %>%
  inner_join(go_to_theme_lookup, by = c("ID", "Ontology_Branch"))

theme_counts <- enriched_themes_df %>%
  group_by(Analysis_Group, Theme, Ontology_Branch) %>%
  summarize(
    Term_Count = n_distinct(ID),
    Best_p.value = min(p.adjust),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(neg_log_p = -log10(Best_p.value))

# ==============================================================================
# 3. PANEL A: BIOLOGICAL PROCESS (BP) HIGH-CONTRAST GRID
# ==============================================================================
bp_themes <- theme_counts %>% filter(Ontology_Branch == "BP")

bp_grid_complete <- expand_grid(
  Analysis_Group = unique(theme_counts$Analysis_Group),
  Theme = unique(structural_anchors$Theme[structural_anchors$Parent_ID %in% bp_lineages$Parent_ID])
) %>%
  left_join(bp_themes, by = c("Analysis_Group", "Theme")) %>%
  mutate(Term_Count = replace_na(Term_Count, 0), neg_log_p = replace_na(neg_log_p, 0))

bp_dotplot <- ggplot(bp_grid_complete, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = Theme)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Term_Count, color = neg_log_p)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0, 9), name = "Number of\nEnriched Terms") +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, name = "-log10(Best p)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray93"),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "gray85", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "High-Contrast Biological Process Functional Landscape",
    subtitle = "Expanded structural subsets to distribute dense metabolic signals",
    x = "Cluster Wave", y = NULL
  )

print(bp_dotplot)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "structural_landscape_bp_high_contrast.pdf"), plot = bp_dotplot, width = 8.5, height = 6, units = "in")

# ==============================================================================
# 4. PANEL B: MOLECULAR FUNCTION (MF) HIGH-CONTRAST GRID
# ==============================================================================
mf_themes <- theme_counts %>% filter(Ontology_Branch == "MF")

mf_grid_complete <- expand_grid(
  Analysis_Group = unique(theme_counts$Analysis_Group),
  Theme = unique(structural_anchors$Theme[structural_anchors$Parent_ID %in% mf_lineages$Parent_ID])
) %>%
  left_join(mf_themes, by = c("Analysis_Group", "Theme")) %>%
  mutate(Term_Count = replace_na(Term_Count, 0), neg_log_p = replace_na(neg_log_p, 0))

mf_dotplot <- ggplot(mf_grid_complete, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = Theme)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Term_Count, color = neg_log_p)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0, 9), name = "Number of\nEnriched Terms") +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "rocket", direction = -1, name = "-log10(Best p)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray93"),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "gray85", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "High-Contrast Molecular Function Functional Landscape",
    subtitle = "Enzymatic and binding sub-classes isolated natively",
    x = "Cluster Wave", y = NULL
  )

print(mf_dotplot)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "structural_landscape_mf_high_contrast.pdf"), plot = mf_dotplot, width = 8.5, height = 6, units = "in")
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

# Ensure the subcategory directory is ready
sub_plots_dir <- file.path(results_dir, "targeted_subcategories")
if (!dir.exists(sub_plots_dir)) dir.create(sub_plots_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# Prepare universal high-resolution metric baseline
raw_high_res_df <- compiled_elim_results %>%
  mutate(
    neg_log_p = -log10(p.adjust),
    Wrapped_GO_Name = str_wrap(as.character(GO_Name), width = 40)
  )

# ==============================================================================
# UNIVERSAL STANDALONE PLOTTING ENGINE
# ==============================================================================
# This engine forces a full-matrix grid layout (filling in zeros for empty waves)
# so you can visually track the exact cluster wave where a pathway turns on.
plot_targeted_subcategory <- function(subset_df, plot_title, filename, color_palette = "mako") {
  if (nrow(subset_df) == 0) {
    message(paste("Skipping", plot_title, "- No enriched terms matched this keyword filter."))
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Guarantee structural grid integrity across all unique clusters in your data
  complete_grid <- expand_grid(
    Analysis_Group = unique(raw_high_res_df$Analysis_Group),
    Wrapped_GO_Name = unique(subset_df$Wrapped_GO_Name)
  ) %>%
    left_join(subset_df, by = c("Analysis_Group", "Wrapped_GO_Name")) %>%
    mutate(neg_log_p = replace_na(neg_log_p, 0))

  sub_heatmap <- ggplot(complete_grid, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = reorder(Wrapped_GO_Name, neg_log_p))) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = neg_log_p), color = "white", lwd = 0.4) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = color_palette, direction = -1, name = "-log10(p)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9, lineheight = 0.85, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = plot_title,
      subtitle = "High-Resolution Elim Term Sub-Slices Across Waves",
      x = "Cluster Wave", y = NULL
    )

  # Save clean layout vectors
  ggsave(file.path(sub_plots_dir, paste0(filename, ".pdf")),
    plot = sub_heatmap, width = 7.5, height = max(3, nrow(subset_df) * 0.35 + 2), units = "in"
  )

  return(sub_heatmap)
}

# 1. AMINO ACID SUBCATEGORY EXTRACTIONS (BP & MF Combined)
# ==============================================================================
message("Extracting targeted Amino Acid subcategories...")

# --- A. Branched-Chain Amino Acids (BCAA) ---
bcaa_terms <- raw_high_res_df %>%
  filter(str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)isoleucine|leucine|valine|branched-chain"))

plot_targeted_subcategory(bcaa_terms, "Branched-Chain Amino Acid (BCAA) Tracks", "sub_bp_bcaa", "mako")


# --- B. Aromatic Amino Acids ---
aromatic_terms <- raw_high_res_df %>%
  filter(str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)tryptophan|tyrosine|phenylalanine|aromatic amino acid"))

plot_targeted_subcategory(aromatic_terms, "Aromatic Amino Acid Modules", "sub_bp_aromatic_aa", "mako")


# --- C. Sulfur-Containing & Nitrogen-Core Amino Acids ---
# Catches primary regulatory vectors like Glutamine/Glutamate and Methionine/Cysteine
nitrogen_sulfur_aa_terms <- raw_high_res_df %>%
  filter(str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)glutamine|glutamate|arginine|methionine|cysteine|sulfur amino acid"))

plot_targeted_subcategory(nitrogen_sulfur_aa_terms, "Core Nitrogen & Sulfur Amino Acids", "sub_bp_nitrogen_sulfur_aa", "mako")

# ==============================================================================
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

# Ensure output directory paths are ready
sub_plots_dir <- file.path(results_dir, "targeted_subcategories")
if (!dir.exists(sub_plots_dir)) dir.create(sub_plots_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. COMPILE ALL AMINO ACID TRACKS WITH SUB-GROUP TAGS
# ==============================================================================
message("Compiling combined amino acid landscapes...")

combined_aa_data <- raw_high_res_df %>%
  mutate(
    # Assign specific sub-group facets using strict regex matches
    AA_Subcategory = case_when(
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)isoleucine|leucine|valine|branched-chain") ~ "Branched-Chain (BCAA)",
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)phenylalanine|tyrosine|tryptophan|histidine|aromatic|shikimate|chorismate") ~ "Cyclic & Aromatic",
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)glutamine|glutamate|arginine|methionine|cysteine|sulfur") ~ "Core Nitrogen & Sulfur",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  # Drop anything that didn't match our target amino acid categories
  filter(!is.na(AA_Subcategory))

# ==============================================================================
# 2. ENFORCE FULL MATRIX CROSS-GRID INTEGRITY
# ==============================================================================
# This step ensures that every child term is mapped against every single cluster wave,
# filling in zeros for empty waves so you can clearly see when a pathway turns on.
complete_aa_grid <- expand_grid(
  Analysis_Group = unique(raw_high_res_df$Analysis_Group),
  Wrapped_GO_Name = unique(combined_aa_data$Wrapped_GO_Name)
) %>%
  # Bring back the metadata and subcategory labels
  left_join(distinct(combined_aa_data, Wrapped_GO_Name, AA_Subcategory), by = "Wrapped_GO_Name") %>%
  # Bring back the actual statistical results
  left_join(combined_aa_data, by = c("Analysis_Group", "Wrapped_GO_Name", "AA_Subcategory")) %>%
  mutate(neg_log_p = replace_na(neg_log_p, 0))

# ==============================================================================
# 3. GENERATE THE FACETED COMBINED GRID FIGURE
# ==============================================================================
# Determine dynamic chart canvas height based on the number of unique matching terms
total_unique_terms <- length(unique(complete_aa_grid$Wrapped_GO_Name))
dynamic_height <- max(4, (total_unique_terms * 0.3) + 2)

combined_aa_plot <- ggplot(complete_aa_grid, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = reorder(Wrapped_GO_Name, neg_log_p))) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = neg_log_p), color = "white", lwd = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, name = "-log10(p)") +

  # FACETING ENGINE: Splits your categories into distinct vertical panels
  # scales = "free_y" ensures panels only show rows belonging to that specific category
  facet_grid(AA_Subcategory ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8.5, lineheight = 0.85, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),

    # Format the panel header labels on the right-hand side
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold", size = 10, hjust = 0),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = "gray85", linewidth = 0.5),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(0.5, "lines")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Comprehensive Amino Acid Metabolic Profile",
    subtitle = "High-Resolution Functional Waves Grouped by Biochemical Subclass",
    x = "Cluster Wave",
    y = NULL
  )

# Output and write to storage
print(combined_aa_plot)
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(sub_plots_dir, "combined_amino_acid_landscape.pdf"),
  plot = combined_aa_plot,
  width = 9.5,
  height = dynamic_height,
  units = "in"
)

message(paste("Combined amino acid panel successfully saved. Output height adjusted to:", dynamic_height, "inches."))
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# UPDATED FIGURE 2: BIOLOGICALLY GROUPED Y-AXIS (NITROGEN & SULFUR)
# ==============================================================================
message("Generating Figure 2 with biologically sorted Y-axis clusters...")

fig2_data <- raw_high_res_df %>%
  mutate(
    Facet_Group = case_when(
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)glutamine|glutamate|arginine|nitrogen|urea") ~ "Core Nitrogen Metabolism",
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)methionine|cysteine|sulfur|homocysteine|iron-sulfur|fe-s") ~ "Sulfur Amino Acids",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Facet_Group))

# Define the full matrix cross-grid to preserve tracking integrity
grid_fig2 <- expand_grid(
  Analysis_Group = unique(raw_high_res_df$Analysis_Group),
  Wrapped_GO_Name = unique(fig2_data$Wrapped_GO_Name)
) %>%
  left_join(distinct(fig2_data, Wrapped_GO_Name, Facet_Group, GO_Name), by = "Wrapped_GO_Name") %>%
  left_join(fig2_data, by = c("Analysis_Group", "Wrapped_GO_Name", "Facet_Group", "GO_Name")) %>%
  mutate(
    neg_log_p = replace_na(neg_log_p, 0),
    Wrapped_Facet = str_wrap(Facet_Group, width = 15)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE BIOLOGICAL SORTING ENGINE
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# REFINED BIOLOGICAL SORTING ENGINE (Strict Glutamate vs. Glutamine Separation)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
y_axis_sorter <- grid_fig2 %>%
  distinct(Wrapped_GO_Name, GO_Name, Facet_Group) %>%
  mutate(
    # Assign narrow, distinct decimal steps to separate twins while keeping them adjacent
    Micro_Cluster = case_when(
      # --- Nitrogen Sub-groups ---
      Facet_Group == "Core Nitrogen Metabolism" & str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)glutamate") ~ 1.11, # Glutamate block
      Facet_Group == "Core Nitrogen Metabolism" & str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)glutamine") ~ 1.12, # Glutamine block
      Facet_Group == "Core Nitrogen Metabolism" & str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)argin") ~ 1.20, # Arginine family
      Facet_Group == "Core Nitrogen Metabolism" & str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)urea") ~ 1.30, # Urea cycle
      Facet_Group == "Core Nitrogen Metabolism" ~ 1.40, # General Nitrogen

      # --- Sulfur & Iron-Sulfur Sub-groups ---
      Facet_Group == "Sulfur Amino Acids" & str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)methion") ~ 2.10, # Methionine
      Facet_Group == "Sulfur Amino Acids" & str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)cyst") ~ 2.20, # Cysteine
      Facet_Group == "Sulfur Amino Acids" & str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)iron|fe-s|iron-") ~ 2.30, # Iron-Sulfur clusters
      Facet_Group == "Sulfur Amino Acids" ~ 2.40 # General Sulfur
    )
  ) %>%
  # Arrange forces the factor levels to stack exactly by this order on your plot
  arrange(Facet_Group, Micro_Cluster, GO_Name)

# Lock this exact structural sequence into the ggplot factor engine
grid_fig2$Wrapped_GO_Name <- factor(
  grid_fig2$Wrapped_GO_Name,
  levels = unique(y_axis_sorter$Wrapped_GO_Name)
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

h2 <- max(4, (length(unique(grid_fig2$Wrapped_GO_Name)) * 0.3) + 2)

# Note: We remove the reorder() function from the y-axis mapping here
# because mapping a pre-ordered Factor directly respects its native levels!
plot_fig2_grouped <- ggplot(grid_fig2, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = Wrapped_GO_Name)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = neg_log_p), color = "white", lwd = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "rocket", direction = -1, name = "-log10(p)") +
  facet_grid(Wrapped_Facet ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8.5, lineheight = 0.85, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 90, face = "bold", size = 9.5, lineheight = 0.9, vjust = 0.5),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = "gray85", linewidth = 0.5),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 2: Macronutrient & Defense Core Pathways",
    subtitle = "Y-Axis organized hierarchically by chemical subclass",
    x = "Cluster Wave",
    y = NULL
  )

ggsave(file.path(sub_plots_dir, "figure_2_nitrogen_and_sulfur.pdf"), plot = plot_fig2_grouped, width = 9, height = h2, units = "in")
message("Figure 2 updated and saved successfully.")
```

```{r}
# FIGURE 3: EXPANDED LANDSCAPE (FIGURE 1 + OTHER AMINO ACIDS)

message("Generating Figure 3 (Figure 1 + Other Amino Acids)...")

fig3_data <- raw_high_res_df %>%
  # Filter for any general amino acid infrastructure term
  filter(str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)amino acid|peptide|aminotransferase|isoleucine|leucine|valine|phenylalanine|tyrosine|tryptophan|histidine|shikimate")) %>%
  # Filter out explicit Nitrogen and Sulfur terms to keep this subset mathematically unmixed
  filter(!ID %in% fig2_data$ID) %>%
  mutate(
    Facet_Group = case_when(
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)isoleucine|leucine|valine|branched-chain") ~ "Branched-Chain (BCAA)",
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)phenylalanine|tyrosine|tryptophan|histidine|aromatic|shikimate|chorismate") ~ "Cyclic & Aromatic",
      # Categorizing the "Other" components
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)polyamine|putrescine|spermidine|cadaverine|lysine") ~ "Polyamines & Lysine Modulators",
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)glycine|serine|threonine|alanine|aspartate") ~ "Small & Aliphatic Modulators",
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)proline|cell wall|peptidoglycan|osmoprotect") ~ "Osmoprotection & Proline",
      TRUE ~ "General AA Transport & Housekeeping"
    )
  )

grid_fig3 <- expand_grid(
  Analysis_Group = unique(raw_high_res_df$Analysis_Group),
  Wrapped_GO_Name = unique(fig3_data$Wrapped_GO_Name)
) %>%
  left_join(distinct(fig3_data, Wrapped_GO_Name, Facet_Group), by = "Wrapped_GO_Name") %>%
  left_join(fig3_data, by = c("Analysis_Group", "Wrapped_GO_Name", "Facet_Group")) %>%
  mutate(
    neg_log_p = replace_na(neg_log_p, 0),
    Wrapped_Facet = str_wrap(Facet_Group, width = 15)
  )

h3 <- max(4.5, (length(unique(grid_fig3$Wrapped_GO_Name)) * 0.3) + 2)

plot_fig3 <- ggplot(grid_fig3, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = reorder(Wrapped_GO_Name, neg_log_p))) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = neg_log_p), color = "white", lwd = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "cividis", direction = -1, name = "-log10(p)") +
  facet_grid(Wrapped_Facet ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8.5, lineheight = 0.85, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 90, face = "bold", size = 9.5, lineheight = 0.9, vjust = 0.5),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = "gray85", linewidth = 0.5),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
  ) +
  labs(title = "Figure 3: Comprehensive Profile & Structural Modulators", x = "Cluster Wave", y = NULL)

ggsave(file.path(sub_plots_dir, "figure_3_expanded_amino_landscape.pdf"), plot = plot_fig3, width = 9.5, height = h3, units = "in")

message("All three distinct figures have been processed and saved successfully.")
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
message("Compiling Figure 4 using a strict chemical-class separation strategy...")

fig4_chem_isolated <- compiled_elim_results %>%
  filter(Ontology_Branch == "BP") %>%
  mutate(
    # Keep full raw text strings for formal compliance
    Clean_GO_Name = GO_Name,
    neg_log_p = -log10(p.adjust),
    Wrapped_GO_Name = str_wrap(Clean_GO_Name, width = 40)
  ) %>%
  # STRATEGY: Sort strictly by chemical functional groups, forcing a clean divide
  mutate(
    Facet_Group = case_when(
      # Group 1: Physical Membrane Adaptations
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)unsaturated|cyclopropane|desaturase|fluidity") ~ "1. Fluidity & Stress Adaptation",

      # Group 2: True Membrane Phospholipid Head Groups
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)phosphatidyl|cardiolipin|glycerolipid|phospholipid") ~ "2. Phospholipid Head Groups",

      # Group 3: Outer Membrane Armor & Envelope Structural Lipids
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)lipid A|lipopolysaccharide|teichoic|outer membrane lipid") ~ "3. Outer Envelope Armor",

      # Group 4: Pure Carbon-Chain Elongation (Strictly excludes amino/protein terms)
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)fatty acid|acyl-carrier|acyl-coa|malonyl") &
        !str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)protein|amino acid|peptide|ribosom|translation|biotin|lipoic") ~ "4. Pure Fatty Acid Chains",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  # Drop anything that doesn't fit into our clean chemical definitions
  filter(!is.na(Facet_Group))
```

```{r}
message("Compiling Figure 4 using a strict chemical-class separation strategy...")

fig4_chem_isolated <- compiled_elim_results %>%
  filter(Ontology_Branch == "BP") %>%
  mutate(
    # Keep full raw text strings for formal compliance
    Clean_GO_Name = GO_Name,
    neg_log_p = -log10(p.adjust),
    Wrapped_GO_Name = str_wrap(Clean_GO_Name, width = 40)
  ) %>%
  # STRATEGY: Sort strictly by chemical functional groups, forcing a clean divide
  mutate(
    Facet_Group = case_when(
      # Group 1: Expanded Fluidity & Physical Membrane Adaptations
      # Catches cold/heat adaptations, homeoviscous responses, and double-bond modifications
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)unsaturated|cyclopropane|desaturase|fluidity|temperature compensation|cold acclimation|heat shock.*membrane") ~ "1. Fluidity & Stress Adaptation",

      # Group 2: Expanded Head Groups & Backbones
      # Captures Cardolipin plus all core bacterial glycerolipid assembly roots
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)phosphatidyl|cardiolipin|glycerolipid|phospholipid|diacylglycerol|glycerol-3-phosphate|cdp-diacylglycerol|serine decarboxylase") ~ "2. Phospholipid Head Groups",

      # Group 3: Expanded Outer Envelope Armor
      # Captures Lipid A, LPS, Teichoic acids, Lipoproteins, and Mycolic architectures
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)lipid A|lipopolysaccharide|teichoic|lipoprotein|outer membrane lipid|cell envelope|peptidoglycan.*lipid|lipid-linked oligosaccharide") ~ "3. Outer Envelope Armor",

      # Group 4: Pure Carbon-Chain Elongation (Strictly isolated from proteins/amino acids)
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)fatty acid|acyl-carrier|acyl-coa|malonyl|ketoacyl") &
        !str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)protein|amino acid|peptide|ribosom|translation|biotin|lipoic") ~ "4. Pure Fatty Acid Chains",
```

```{r USE_THIS}
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)fatty acid|acyl-coa|synthase|dehydrogenase|c-acyltransferase|ligase|hydrolase") &

      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)lipid.*transporter|transmembrane.*lipid|glycerophosphodiester") ~ "2. Lipid Translocation Machinery",
```

```{r facet-GO}
# ==============================================================================
# FIGURE 4: AUTOMATED HEATMAP CLUSTERING VIA HIERARCHICAL DISTANCE
# ==============================================================================
message("Rebuilding Figure 4: Calculating automated hierarchical clustering...")

# 1. PREPARE THE DATA AND APPLY STRING TRUNCATION
fig4_raw_data <- compiled_elim_results %>%
  filter(Ontology_Branch %in% c("BP", "MF")) %>%
  mutate(
    # Clean up labels per your instructions
    Truncated_GO_Name = str_remove(GO_Name, ",.*$"),
    Clean_GO_Name = str_remove(Truncated_GO_Name, "\\s+activity$"),
    neg_log_p = -log10(p.adjust),
    Wrapped_GO_Name = str_wrap(Clean_GO_Name, width = 45)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Facet_Group = case_when(
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)fatty acid|acyl-coa|synthase|dehydrogenase|c-acyltransferase|ligase|hydrolase") &
        !str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)targeting|localization|tRNA|translation|protein acylation|transporter") ~ "1. Fatty Acid Lifecycle",
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)lipid.*transporter|transmembrane.*lipid|glycerophosphodiester") ~ "2. Lipid Translocation",
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)cell wall") ~ "3. Outer Envelope Armor",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Facet_Group))

# 2. RUN MATHEMATICAL HIERARCHICAL CLUSTERING (Performs the placement)
# Pivot the data into a wide matrix (Terms x Waves) to compute distance profiles
clustering_matrix <- fig4_raw_data %>%
  select(Wrapped_GO_Name, Analysis_Group, neg_log_p) %>%
  # Handle any potential duplicate rows gracefully
  distinct(Wrapped_GO_Name, Analysis_Group, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Analysis_Group, values_from = neg_log_p, values_fill = 0) %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("Wrapped_GO_Name")

# Compute Euclidean distance and cluster via Complete Linkage
row_distances <- dist(clustering_matrix, method = "euclidean")
row_dendrogram <- hclust(row_distances, method = "complete")

# Extract the mathematically optimal row order
ordered_terms <- rownames(clustering_matrix)[row_dendrogram$order]

# Lock the data frame factor levels to match the dendrogram order
fig4_raw_data$Wrapped_GO_Name <- factor(fig4_raw_data$Wrapped_GO_Name, levels = ordered_terms)

# 3. ENFORCE CROSS-GRID MATRIX INTEGRITY
grid_fig4_clustered <- expand_grid(
  Analysis_Group = unique(compiled_elim_results$Analysis_Group),
  Wrapped_GO_Name = unique(fig4_raw_data$Wrapped_GO_Name)
) %>%
  left_join(distinct(fig4_raw_data, Wrapped_GO_Name, Facet_Group), by = "Wrapped_GO_Name") %>%
  left_join(fig4_raw_data, by = c("Analysis_Group", "Wrapped_GO_Name", "Facet_Group")) %>%
  mutate(
    neg_log_p = replace_na(neg_log_p, 0),
    Wrapped_Facet = str_wrap(Facet_Group, width = 18)
  )

h4_cluster <- max(4.5, (length(unique(grid_fig4_clustered$Wrapped_GO_Name)) * 0.35) + 2)

# 4. PLOT ENGINE
plot_fig4_clustered <- ggplot(grid_fig4_clustered, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = Wrapped_GO_Name)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = neg_log_p), color = "white", lwd = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "rocket", direction = -1, name = "-log10(p)") +
  # scales = "free_y" and space = "free_y" respect the cluster order inside each facet panel
  facet_grid(Wrapped_Facet ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8.5, lineheight = 0.85, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
```

```{r cluster-both}
# ==============================================================================
# FIGURE 4: TWO-DIMENSIONAL AUTOMATED HIERARCHICAL HEATMAP
# ==============================================================================
message("Rebuilding Figure 4: Automating BOTH row and column placement...")

# 1. CLEAN AND PREPARE DATA
fig4_dual_data <- compiled_elim_results %>%
  filter(Ontology_Branch %in% c("BP", "MF")) %>%
  mutate(
    Truncated_GO_Name = str_remove(GO_Name, ",.*$"),
    Clean_GO_Name = str_remove(Truncated_GO_Name, "\\s+activity$"),
    neg_log_p = -log10(p.adjust),
    Wrapped_GO_Name = str_wrap(Clean_GO_Name, width = 45)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Facet_Group = case_when(
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)fatty acid|acyl-coa|synthase|dehydrogenase|c-acyltransferase|ligase|hydrolase") &
        !str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)targeting|localization|tRNA|translation|protein acylation|transporter") ~ "1. Fatty Acid Lifecycle",
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)lipid.*transporter|transmembrane.*lipid|glycerophosphodiester") ~ "2. Lipid Translocation",
      str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)cell wall") ~ "3. Outer Envelope Armor",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Facet_Group))

# 2. GENERATE THE WIDE MATRIX FOR DUAL CLUSTERING
clustering_matrix <- fig4_dual_data %>%
  select(Wrapped_GO_Name, Analysis_Group, neg_log_p) %>%
  distinct(Wrapped_GO_Name, Analysis_Group, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Analysis_Group, values_from = neg_log_p, values_fill = 0) %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("Wrapped_GO_Name")

# --- AXIS 1: AUTOMATE VERTICAL ROW ORDER (GO TERMS) ---
row_distances <- dist(clustering_matrix, method = "euclidean")
row_dendrogram <- hclust(row_distances, method = "complete")
ordered_rows <- rownames(clustering_matrix)[row_dendrogram$order]

# --- AXIS 2: AUTOMATE HORIZONTAL COLUMN ORDER (SCATTERPLOT CLUSTERS) ---
# Transpose the matrix to cluster columns based on their GO term enrichment profiles
col_distances <- dist(t(clustering_matrix), method = "euclidean")
col_dendrogram <- hclust(col_distances, method = "complete")
ordered_columns <- colnames(clustering_matrix)[col_dendrogram$order]

# 3. APPLY FORCED ORDER TO BOTH AXES AS STRICT FACTORS
fig4_dual_data$Wrapped_GO_Name <- factor(fig4_dual_data$Wrapped_GO_Name, levels = ordered_rows)
fig4_dual_data$Analysis_Group <- factor(fig4_dual_data$Analysis_Group, levels = ordered_columns)

# 4. ENFORCE CROSS-GRID MATRIX INTEGRITY
grid_fig4_dual <- expand_grid(
  Analysis_Group = factor(ordered_columns, levels = ordered_columns),
  Wrapped_GO_Name = factor(ordered_rows, levels = ordered_rows)
) %>%
  left_join(distinct(fig4_dual_data, Wrapped_GO_Name, Facet_Group), by = "Wrapped_GO_Name") %>%
  left_join(fig4_dual_data, by = c("Analysis_Group", "Wrapped_GO_Name", "Facet_Group")) %>%
  mutate(
    neg_log_p = replace_na(neg_log_p, 0),
    Wrapped_Facet = str_wrap(Facet_Group, width = 18)
  )

h4_dual <- max(4.5, (length(unique(grid_fig4_dual$Wrapped_GO_Name)) * 0.35) + 2)

# 5. PLOT DUAL-AUTOMATED ENGINE
plot_fig4_dual <- ggplot(grid_fig4_dual, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = Wrapped_GO_Name)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = neg_log_p), color = "white", lwd = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "rocket", direction = -1, name = "-log10(p)") +
  facet_grid(Wrapped_Facet ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8.5, lineheight = 0.85, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 90, face = "bold", size = 9.5, lineheight = 0.9, vjust = 0.5),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = "gray85", linewidth = 0.5),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(0.6, "lines")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 4: Bidimensional Clustering of Lipid Metabolic Phenotypes",
    subtitle = "Fully Automated: Columns grouped by scatterplot behavior profile; Rows grouped by functional similarity",
    x = "Scatterplot Behavior Groups (Ordered by Profile Proximity)",
    y = NULL
  )

print(plot_fig4_dual)

ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "targeted_subcategories", "figure_4_fatty_acid_lifecycle.pdf"),
  plot = plot_fig4_dual, width = 10.5, height = h4_dual, units = "in"
)

message("Bidirectionally clustered Figure 4 successfully plotted.")
plot_fig4_dual
```

```{r}
message("Rendering high-contrast biclustered heatmap to screen...")

# 1. PREPARE THE RAW EXTRACTION
fig4_pure_data <- raw_lipid_df %>%
  mutate(
    neg_log_p = -log10(p.adjust),
    # Maintain names strictly for internal clustering matrix math
    Wrapped_GO_Name = str_wrap(GO_Name, width = 50)
  )

all_possible_clusters <- unique(compiled_elim_results$Analysis_Group)

# 2. PIVOT TO WIDE MATRIX AND GENERATE TREES
pure_matrix <- fig4_pure_data %>%
  select(Wrapped_GO_Name, Analysis_Group, neg_log_p) %>%
  distinct(Wrapped_GO_Name, Analysis_Group, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  tidyr::complete(Wrapped_GO_Name, Analysis_Group = all_possible_clusters, fill = list(neg_log_p = 0)) %>%

  tibble::column_to_rownames("Wrapped_GO_Name")

# Compute Hierarchical Trees
row_dist <- dist(pure_matrix, method = "euclidean")
row_hc <- hclust(row_dist, method = "complete")
pure_ordered_rows <- rownames(pure_matrix)[row_hc$order]

col_dist <- dist(t(pure_matrix), method = "euclidean")
col_hc <- hclust(col_dist, method = "complete")
pure_ordered_cols <- colnames(pure_matrix)[col_hc$order]

# 3. LOCK FACTOR AXES
fig4_pure_data$Wrapped_GO_Name <- factor(fig4_pure_data$Wrapped_GO_Name, levels = pure_ordered_rows)
fig4_pure_data$Analysis_Group <- factor(fig4_pure_data$Analysis_Group, levels = pure_ordered_cols)

# 4. ENFORCE INTEGRITY ACROSS THE COMPLETED GRID MATRIX
grid_pure <- expand_grid(
  Analysis_Group = factor(pure_ordered_cols, levels = pure_ordered_cols),
  Wrapped_GO_Name = factor(pure_ordered_rows, levels = pure_ordered_rows)
) %>%
  left_join(fig4_pure_data, by = c("Analysis_Group", "Wrapped_GO_Name")) %>%
  mutate(neg_log_p = replace_na(neg_log_p, 0))

# 5. HEATMAP PLOT ENGINE (CLEANED & CONTRAST ADJUSTED)
plot_fig4_pure_clean <- ggplot(grid_pure, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = Wrapped_GO_Name)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = neg_log_p), color = "white", lwd = 0.1) +

  # COLOR CONTRAST FILTER: Forces 0 to be a neutral background color,
  # while active values blend smoothly from warm orange to bright yellow/white.
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = c("gray96", "#3b0f70", "#8c2981", "#de4968", "#fe9f6d", "#fcfdbf"),
    values = scales::rescale(c(0, 0.001, 2, 4, 8, max(grid_pure$neg_log_p, na.rm = TRUE))),
    name = "-log10(p)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    # REMOVED: Completely drops the text and tick spacing on the y-axis
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Pure Lipid Biclustering Profile (Clean View)",
    subtitle = "Zero-Masked Palette: Shifting background noise to isolate true kinetic blocks",
    x = "Scatterplot Phenotype Clusters (Automated Ordering)",
    y = NULL
  )

# Display to screen
print(plot_fig4_pure_clean)
```

```{r}
    # Clean up labels per your instructions

  ) %>%
```

```{r}
      "valine|leucine|isoleucine|branched-chain|",
      # Aromatic
      "tryptophan|phenylalanine|tyrosine|aromatic|chorismate|",
      # Sulfur & Basic/Other Core Specifics
      "methionine|cysteine|arginine|lysine|histidine|glutamate|glutamine|",
      # Interconversion / General specific lines
      "aspartate|asparagine|proline|serine|threonine|glycine|alanine"
    ))
  ) %>%
  # Aggressively strip out generic translation, tRNA charging, and structural ribosome noise
  filter(!str_detect(GO_Name, "(?i)tRNA|translation|ribosom|peptide|proteolyt|peptidase"))

# Get an absolute master list of every cluster wave present in your analysis
all_possible_clusters <- unique(compiled_elim_results$Analysis_Group)

  tidyr::complete(Wrapped_GO_Name, Analysis_Group = all_possible_clusters, fill = list(neg_log_p = 0)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Analysis_Group, values_from = neg_log_p, values_fill = 0) %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("Wrapped_GO_Name")

# Check if data exists after strict filtration to avoid clustering empty matrices
if (nrow(matrix_aa_specific) > 1) {
  # --- MATHEMATICAL AXIS 1: AUTOMATE VERTICAL ROWS (GO TERMS) ---
  row_dist_spec <- dist(matrix_aa_specific, method = "euclidean")
  row_hc_spec <- hclust(row_dist_spec, method = "complete")
  ordered_rows_spec <- rownames(matrix_aa_specific)[row_hc_spec$order]

  # --- MATHEMATICAL AXIS 2: AUTOMATE HORIZONTAL COLUMNS (SCATTERPLOT CLUSTERS) ---
  col_dist_spec <- dist(t(matrix_aa_specific), method = "euclidean")
  col_hc_spec <- hclust(col_dist_spec, method = "complete")
  ordered_columns_spec <- colnames(matrix_aa_specific)[col_hc_spec$order]

  # 3. INTERLOCK BOTH AXES AS COMPLETED HIERARCHICAL FACTORS
  fig5_aa_specific$Wrapped_GO_Name <- factor(fig5_aa_specific$Wrapped_GO_Name, levels = ordered_rows_spec)
  fig5_aa_specific$Analysis_Group <- factor(fig5_aa_specific$Analysis_Group, levels = ordered_columns_spec)

  # 4. ENFORCE TOTAL CROSS-GRID INTEGRITY FOR PLOTTING
  grid_spec_aa <- expand_grid(
    Analysis_Group = factor(ordered_columns_spec, levels = ordered_columns_spec),
    Wrapped_GO_Name = factor(ordered_rows_spec, levels = ordered_rows_spec)
  ) %>%
    left_join(fig5_aa_specific, by = c("Analysis_Group", "Wrapped_GO_Name")) %>%
    mutate(neg_log_p = replace_na(neg_log_p, 0))

  # Dynamically scale canvas height based on the targeted row volume (0.16 inch compact scaling)
  h5_spec_aa <- max(5, (length(unique(grid_spec_aa$Wrapped_GO_Name)) * 0.16) + 1.5)

  # 5. GENERATE UNFACETED CONTINUOUS HEATMAP
  plot_fig5_spec_aa <- ggplot(grid_spec_aa, aes(x = Analysis_Group, y = Wrapped_GO_Name)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = neg_log_p), color = "white", lwd = 0.2) +

    # Zero-masked high-contrast color palette mapping to pinpoint active blocks
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colors = c("gray96", "#3b0f70", "#8c2981", "#de4968", "#fe9f6d", "#fcfdbf"),
      values = scales::rescale(c(0, 0.001, 2, 4, 8, max(grid_spec_aa$neg_log_p, na.rm = TRUE))),

    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +

      title = "Biclustering of Granular Amino Acid Pathways",
      subtitle = "Targeted Matrix: Specific biosynthesis & breakdown chains ordered by behavior profile",

    )

  # Display to screen interface
  print(plot_fig5_spec_aa)

  # 6. SAVE OUTPUT
  ggsave(
```
